Sports.title: Social Media: Ben Sulayem defends Gasly after latest abuse from Colapinto fans | Brief
Sports.content:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has condemned the online abuse directed at Pierre Gasly by supporters of his team mate.

Gasly briefly delayed Franco Colapinto during the latter stages of the Spanish Grand Prix two weeks ago. The driver and his family have since received abusive messages on social media.

“The online abuse directed at Pierre Gasly and his family is completely unacceptable,” said Ben Sulayem in a post. “Pierre has my full support, and I strongly condemn this behaviour. No driver, official, volunteer or fan should have to face this.

“Incidents like this are why I founded the United Against Online Abuse initiative. We simply cannot accept online hate within our sport and we all have a responsibility – governing bodies, teams, drivers, fans and social media platforms – to challenge this behaviour and create an environment built on respect.”

Colapinto’s supporters have been repeatedly accused of aiming abuse at drivers and other figures in the sport, including Jack Doohan last year, his own team this year and the FIA’s stewards last month.

“Competition and passion are at the heart of motorsport, but abuse has no place in it,” Ben Sulayem added. “We must continue to stand together and take meaningful action to protect everyone in our sporting community.”

Sports.title: Ocon confirms he is a “free agent” for 2027 as rumours link Camara to Haas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon looks set to leave Haas at the end of the season as the driver admitted he is a “free agent” for 2027.

The 30-year-old joined the team from Alpine last year. He was out-scored by rookie team mate Oliver Bearman last year and lies behind his team mate in the standings.

“At the moment I’m definitely a free agent for next year,” said Ocon in Baku. “[There are] all these discussions and there are certain topics in the background that are out of my control at this moment. So I’m focused on the track, trying to deliver the best I can and getting the result that this team deserves.”

Neither Haas driver has scored since Ocon’s ninth-place finish in Monaco.

Ocon said he’s been “really happy with my personal performance” lately. “I think I’ve been getting the maximum out of the car for quite a while now and we’ve never doubted about it.

“Of course, when the car is working, it helps [you] to get something better. When the inconsistencies of the cars are here, where you struggle more, you don’t look as good.

“But I know that I’m exploiting the maximum of the package that I have every single time. So that’s strong.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ocon ran 10th at the last round in Madrid prior to his pit stop, but fell to 11th at the finish.

“I’m the last one to have scored for the team in Monaco, but it’s been a while. But we were [running] in the points in Madrid, we got both Audis at the start, and we lost it in the pit lane. So this is something we will get stronger on now. But it was a very strong weekend.

“I’m happy with my performance. So we need to keep going here, hopefully have another strong one. There’s usually things happening on this track so I’m looking forward to driving here.”

Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara, who is currently second in the Formula 2 standings, has been linked to the team. Bearman is also part of Ferrari’s young driver programme.

Sports.title: Antonelli has “perfect driving style” for 2026 cars – Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is enjoying an extraordinarily successful second season in Formula 1 because his driving style works perfectly with the current generation of cars, says his team mate.

George Russell is Antonelli’s closest rival at the top of the championship standings, but the second-year driver is 81 points ahead. This is a sharp contrast to last year, when Russell out-scored Antonelli by 319 points to 150.

While Russell said Antonelli’s ability was clear before this season, he believes the reduction in aerodynamic downforce and grip this year has played to his team mate’s strengths.

“Of course Kimi is extremely talented,” said Russell. “He’s an incredible driver and has been fast in his whole career.

“I think his driving style is very similar to what he had last year and I think with just how things have fallen this year, it’s kind of the perfect driving style for these cars.”

Russell believes the same is true of other drivers, including Lando Norris, who is the only driver to have won more than one round this season.

“If you look last year, there are definitely trends,” said Russell. “If you look at Brazil last year, Kimi had a really strong race and Lando won in Brazil, and they’re two drivers who are always very strong on the low grip tracks and they’re two drivers who are arguably the best-performing drivers of this season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s an amazing driver and he was of course doing extremely well last year as well. Let’s see next year if it changes or not, but certainly his natural driving style suits very well for this regulation.”

Charles Leclerc echoed Russell’s view that Antonelli’s potential was clear despite his patchy rookie campaign last year.

“I wish I knew, but clearly he’s doing something that works very well,” said Leclerc. “But to be honest, it’s not that it comes as a complete surprise.

“If I look at Kimi going through the junior ranks, I think it was quite clear for everybody that he had something very special. If you look obviously at his first year in Formula 1, I think he probably faced challenges – it is not up to me to go into detail, I don’t know, but surely he had some struggles in the first year – but this year has been extremely impressive. I mean, from the first race to now, he’s been perfect and driving at a very high level against a driver that I rate extremely high as well, which is George. So he’s doing an incredible job.”

However Leclerc said there is only so much he can tell about Antonelli’s qualities from outside the Mercedes team.

“To [tell] you exactly why he’s so fast, and why he is outstandingly fast this year compared to last year, is very difficult for me. We are all here analysing the data of everybody but we can only go up to a certain amount of detail, then you really need the data of the actual car to dig into more detail.

“So it’s difficult. But his laps look a lot on the limit but somehow he manages to do the lap when it counts and that’s been very impressive to watch.”

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Faces Cardiff Payday Reality
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he’ll fight Keyshawn Davis in Wales. He also wants the money to remain the same as when the bout was pitched for Madison Square Garden. If Pacquiao–Shakur joins Fury–Joshua in Cardiff, that demand becomes much harder to satisfy.

Hitchins says he has accepted the Davis fight and that Keyshawn told him he was ready to sign. He dislikes the proposed move overseas but would make the trip for the opportunity. The opponent isn’t his sticking point. The terms might be.

“As long as the pay is the same, I’m cool,” Hitchins told Sean Zittel and Radio Raheem.

The original plan, by Hitchins’s account, put him and Davis in the co-feature beneath Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in New York. Cardiff changes the audience and the setting. A possible Manny Pacquiao–Shakur Stevenson fight changes the card’s pecking order as well. If that bout is added, Hitchins–Davis would likely sit beneath two much bigger attractions.

Hitchins has every right to ask for the purse he wants. Promoters have to decide what the fight adds at that price. Two skilled Americans meeting at welterweight is an excellent matchup for boxing followers, but Hitchins’s patient style may be a tough sell to a stadium crowd waiting for Fury and Joshua. Twelve rounds of careful jabbing and clinching would put pressure on the event’s pace, especially if his bout runs close to the headliners.

Madison Square Garden would have given Hitchins familiar surroundings and supporters in the building. In Cardiff, he would need to win over a crowd with little reason to favor either American. Davis may have the more crowd pleasing combinations, though he still has to land them against a boxer who excels at controlling distance.

None of this means Hitchins is refusing Wales or that his purse is holding up the deal. No figures have been disclosed, and Pacquiao–Shakur has not been finalized. The offer Hitchins liked in New York may look different on a crowded Cardiff bill. He has accepted the opponent. Now he needs the terms to work.

Hitchins holding out for co-feature money while sitting in the number three slot shows a complete failure to grasp how Zuffa, TKO, and Netflix operate.

Dana White and TKO do not overpay undercard fighters who bring zero ticket sales or subscriptions. They run a business built on leverage. When a card features heavyweight giants like Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua alongside a pairing like Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson, every dollar is already allocated to the top of the marquee. Those headliners drive the subscriptions and pack eighty thousand seats in Cardiff. The third fight on the bill is there to fill airtime, not eat up premium budget.

Hitchins is confusing his personal ambition with actual market value. Fighters slotted third on a mega broadcast do not get multimillion-dollar packages. If he demands the same guarantee he was pitched when he thought he was the primary co-feature in New York, Zuffa and the organizers will simply look past him. Keyshawn wants the fight, but Keyshawn also has promotional backing and mainstream interest.

If Hitchins digs his heels in over money, matchmakers can easily replace him with another welterweight or junior welterweight hungry for global exposure on Netflix. By overplaying his hand, Hitchins risks sitting at home watching Keyshawn fight someone else under the brightest lights in the sport.

Matchmakers have an endless line of hungry contenders ready to take Hitchins’ spot for half the money just to get on a global Netflix stage. If Hitchins walks away over purse demands, nobody is shedding a tear, and the promoters will not hesitate to pivot to a replacement who comes to throw leather.

Keyshawn comes out ahead regardless. If Hitchins drops out, Keyshawn gets matched with an aggressive, fan-friendly welterweight or junior welterweight whom he can likely dismantle in style. Looking explosive on a bill featuring Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua, Manny Pacquiao, and Shakur Stevenson does infinitely more for Keyshawn’s market value than chasing Hitchins around the ring for twelve rounds of clinches and jabs.

For Hitchins, walking away would be career self-sabotage. His style has never drawn mainstream attention or moved live gates. He needs marquee dance partners to stay relevant. Accepting smaller money to fight Keyshawn in Wales is the necessary cost of entry to unlock the division’s real moneymakers.

Beating Keyshawn is Hitchins’ only path to force his way into conversations with the big money names at welterweight. If Hitchins prices himself out now, he shuts the door on all of them [Ryan Garcia, Devin Haney, Teofimo Lopez and Rolando Romero]. He gets left in the cold, relegated to low-profile headline slots on small cards. Taking the fight, taking the pay cut, and taking the trip to Wales is his only real lottery ticket.

Sports.title: Fundora and Hadribeaj Give Fans Little to Talk About
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora promised to burn down Las Vegas. Ermal Hadribeaj promised a hard fight. Both sounded ready during Thursday’s virtual press conference, but the first media push for their October 17 title fight gave casual fans little reason to stop scrolling. That is a problem for a card whose main event already needs an introduction.

Fundora said he intends to extend his three-fight knockout streak. Hadribeaj spoke about the work that earned him a shot at the WBC super welterweight title and what becoming Albania’s first world champion would mean to him. Those stakes are real. Neither man, though, gave the press conference a line that made the matchup feel urgent.

“We’re only focused on this fight. We know that we can’t overlook anyone. We focus on the work and take it one fight at a time,” Fundora said during Thursday’s virtual press conference.

That is sensible preparation from a champion. It is a tough sales pitch. Hadribeaj was equally respectful, calling Fundora “a great guy” and recalling that they met three years ago. His most interesting answer came when he rejected the obvious advice to attack Fundora’s body. He said others have tried it and suggested he has worked on specific answers, but kept those details to himself.

The rest of the card has the same problem. Jermall Charlo was once a name that drew attention on its own. Long stretches out of the ring have cost him that pull, and a bout with Koen Mazoudier offers little to restore it before the opening bell. Their fight had been scheduled for July in Australia before Charlo’s trip fell through; moving it to Las Vegas has given the card a former champion, but not a matchup many fans were asking to see.

Brandon Figueroa’s title defense is harder to understand. He stopped Nick Ball in the final round to win the WBA featherweight belt, a result that should have set up another fight with immediate appeal. Instead, he faces 35-year-old Tomoki Kameda, who lost to IBF champion Angelo Leo in 2025. Kameda is ranked by the WBA, so this is a legitimate title defense. Still, Leo is the opponent who would give fans a clear answer about where Figueroa stands among the featherweight champions.

Fundora and Hadribeaj may produce an excellent fight. Figueroa usually makes opponents work, and Charlo’s return will interest those who have followed him for years. But Thursday was a chance to make people care before October 17. The fighters gave the promoter very little to work with, while the matchmaking left the card’s biggest questions unanswered.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua Fight for WBA Super Title
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are receiving an unearned gift from the World Boxing Association. Neither Briton holds a world title, and their December 11 spectacle in Cardiff on Netflix certainly requires no manufactured hardware to pack a stadium. The sanctioning body is tossing its top heavyweight prize into the ring anyway, staging a brazen demotion of the actual titleholder standing in the wings.

Murat Gassiev did everything asked of him. He earned his position in the ring, collected his status after Oleksandr Usyk vacated, and defended his position by stopping Peter Kadiru in July. His reward is watching the WBA invent a higher tier out of thin air to accommodate two fighters who enter the ring with zero championship claims.

The super champion designation was created to honor unifications and dominant multi-belt reigns. Fury and Joshua possess none of that hardware today. Handing an elite designation to a pair of contenders coming off non-title bouts shreds the integrity of the rankings. The organization relies on discretionary clauses in its rulebook, but pulling bureaucratic rank to vault two big-name fighters past an active titlist exposes pure promotional favoritism.

Commercial convenience drives the maneuver. Attaching a world title to a global Netflix event allows the sanctioning body to secure maximum bout fees and purse percentages capped at five hundred thousand dollars total between both corners. That payday completely derails the campaign the organization spent years trumpeting, abandoning its pledge to eliminate duplicate titles and reduce every division to a single recognized champion.

Cardiff promises massive global exposure, but it leaves the division splintered. The victor will inevitably chase an immediate rematch, an undisputed bout, or walk away into retirement. Gassiev will find zero incentive from the winner to stage a dangerous, low-reward clash.

If the sanctioning body possesses any credibility, it must establish a mandatory deadline ordering the Cardiff winner to face Gassiev within six months. Without an enforceable consolidation order, the super title remains an arbitrary marketing prop manufactured to reward commercial power while the real champion stays shoved to the curb.

Throwing a manufactured Super title onto this Cardiff event is an outright insult to the sport. Neither Fury nor Joshua enters this fight carrying championship momentum. Both were thoroughly solved and dethroned by Oleksandr Usyk, and both have spent the latter stages of their careers surviving shaky outings against fringe opposition rather than beating top-tier contenders.

Inventing a world title specifically for them rewrites the entire definition of what a championship represents. The primary outrage sits squarely with the blatant demotion of Murat Gassiev. The sanctioning body spent years running a public relations victory lap, swearing to clean up its reputation by phasing out multiple champions and establishing one belt per weight class.

That promise evaporated the second Netflix and the Saudi backers dangled a massive live event. Gassiev took care of business in the ring against Pulev and Kadiru, only to be shoved down to secondary status. For the casual viewers tuning in on Netflix, the graphics package will do its job. The broadcast will flash world title belts across the screen, the commentary team will talk about legacy, and the mainstream audience will swallow the idea that the winner is the true king of the heavyweight division.

Hardcore fans know better. A real world title cannot be handed out as a promotional party favor to two aging fighters years past their absolute prime. It degrades the division, reduces the belt to a rented stage prop, and reminds anyone paying close attention that in the heavyweight hierarchy, money and broadcast leverage will always trump genuine athletic merit.

Casual fans will view it as a real world title fight because the television screen tells them to. The mainstream audience does not follow sanctioning body mandates, title unifications, or mandatory rankings. They see two names they recognize from mainstream headlines, a stadium packed with seventy thousand screaming fans. To someone who watches boxing once every two years, whoever walks out of Cardiff with that belt looks like the king.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs  Anthony Joshua Finally Official: December 11 in Cardiff on Netflix
Sports.content:
The British heavyweight rivals will meet at Principality Stadium after a dispute over the venue delayed their long-awaited fight.

Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) and Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) will finally fight on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, live on Netflix. The confirmation ends months of negotiations over where the British heavyweight clash would take place.

The venue dispute is settled. Joshua’s camp had insisted on staging the bout in Britain, while New York’s Madison Square Garden became a serious alternative.

“I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over……..” Turki Alalshikh wrote on X.

Both fighters signed earlier this year. A date and venue remained unresolved, however, allowing the dispute to drag on despite their agreement to face each other. Fury repeatedly blamed Joshua in public and suggested he could pursue a third fight against Oleksandr Usyk.

Dana White said: “For more than a decade, boxing fans have been clamoring for the heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Together, they bring 66 wins, 52 knockouts and multiple heavyweight world titles into the ring. On December 11, two of the biggest heavyweights of this generation finally collide and the winner will take a significant place in heavyweight history.”

Netflix says White and The Ring will collaborate to promote the fight, despite Eddie Hearn’s earlier insistence that White would not be its promoter.

Joshua has boxed at Principality Stadium twice before, stopping Carlos Takam and then outpointing Joseph Parker to add the WBO heavyweight belt to his collection. He returns to face the British rival whose name has followed him through years of callouts and failed negotiations.

Both men came through summer bouts.

Joshua survived two first-round knockdowns against Kristian Prenga in July before stopping him in the second. Fury stopped Mariusz Wach after seven rounds in Thailand that month, having returned in April to outpoint Aslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Those victories kept their meeting alive. Now the former heavyweight champions have a confirmed December date in Britain, with Netflix carrying the broadcast.

Sports.title: Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson Remain in Cardiff Talks
Sports.content:
Manny Pacquiao against Shakur Stevenson remains under discussion for the proposed Anthony Joshua-Tyson Fury card in Cardiff. It would give the event a second major fight, but neither Pacquiao nor Stevenson has received a bout agreement.

BoxingScene’s Lance Pugmire reports that two people connected to the talks say Netflix wants the matchup as part of a “double main event.” December 11 is the date under consideration at Principality Stadium, with December 18 also possible. Pacquiao adviser Jas Mathur told BoxingScene that Pacquiao’s financial terms are still being negotiated.

That leaves a great deal to settle before anyone can call this a fight. The Cardiff show itself has yet to be formally announced, and moving Joshua-Fury from the previously discussed Madison Square Garden setting means assembling the rest of the card around a different venue and date.

Pacquiao-Stevenson would bring two very different attractions to that card. Stevenson, 29, is coming off his January win over Teofimo Lopez and has since signed with Zuffa Boxing. Pacquiao, 47, drew with Mario Barrios in his July 2025 return. His name would draw attention far beyond the usual boxing audience, though the long layoff and age difference would become part of the conversation as soon as the fight was announced.

The proposed pairing also raises a practical question: what weight would they fight at? Pacquiao’s return came at welterweight, while Stevenson’s recent work has been at lighter weights. No weight, number of rounds, or title terms have been announced.

For now, the news is that Pacquiao-Stevenson has survived the reported switch to Cardiff and remains in Netflix’s plans, according to BoxingScene. The decisive development would be agreements reaching both fighters. Until then, it belongs on the list of fights being negotiated, rather than the Joshua-Fury undercard.

Pacquiao turns 48 on December 17. If the fight lands on December 18, Shakur would face him one day after his birthday. Pacquiao won his first world title in 1998, before Shakur turned two.

That age difference makes the matchup a hard sell as a competitive fight. If Shakur wins easily, how much credit does he get for beating a man nearly two decades older? If he boxes his way to a quiet decision, Pacquiao’s name may bring viewers to Netflix, but the fight may give them little reason to watch Shakur again.

Pacquiao’s fame can make this a major event. Turning it into a fight that helps Shakur is another matter. First, both men need to agree to terms; neither has received a bout agreement.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Picks Leonard, But Ray Robinson Set The Harder Standard
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson prefers Sugar Ray Leonard to Sugar Ray Robinson. It is easy to see why. Leonard’s speed, movement, and command of distance resemble the qualities Shakur prizes in his own boxing. But Leonard’s finest wins also required him to fight through danger, and Robinson did that across a schedule neither man came close to matching.

“I like SRL better then I like SRR, This might make my people mad but SRL was one hellavu fighter to me his level was extremely high!!” said Shakur on X.

Stevenson posted that on X on September 22. He had previously called Robinson “buns,” then conceded Robinson was a great fighter and said he had been talking trash. His preference for Leonard is consistent with that view.

Leonard was no fighter who simply ran from trouble. He lost a hard 15 rounds to Roberto Durán, came back to beat him, and stopped Thomas Hearns late in their first fight. His footwork gave him choices; when those fights demanded more, he had offense and resolve to draw upon.

Robinson’s record makes the comparison tougher for Shakur. At age 29, Robinson was 108-1-2 with 72 knockouts. Shakur Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs) has fought 25 times at the same age. Leonard had fought 34. Different eras produced different schedules, but Robinson’s total still speaks to his ability to win, recover, and do it again.

Shakur’s defense is exceptional. What remains unproven is how he would respond if his legs slowed and an opponent forced him to fight for long stretches at close range. Leonard showed he had answers when movement was insufficient. Robinson showed them more than a hundred times before his 29th birthday, backed by power Shakur has yet to display.

Shakur can like Leonard better. If he is judging the full range of what a fighter had to survive and deliver, Robinson deserves a closer look.

Nobody from modern eras, Leonard included, touches what Robinson accomplished by 29.

Robinson was 128-1-2 with 84 knockouts by the time he hit his 30th birthday, and that lone defeat to Jake LaMotta was avenged multiple times over. He was fighting every few weeks, traveling by car or train, taking on rugged contenders in 15-round fights with small gloves and no modern sports science. If Leonard had tried to keep that exact pace against that level of weekly attrition, his body would have broken down even sooner. Leonard had brittle hands and a detached retina by fight 28. Robinson had a jaw made of granite, brutal endurance, and lethal power in both hands.

Shakur picking Leonard makes sense purely through the lens of modern comfort. Leonard represents the blueprint Shakur relates to: the flashy television superstar, the Olympic gold medalist, the master of lateral movement, hand speed, and distance management. Leonard showed that a fighter could dictate terms, generate huge paydays, and maintain an aura without having to fight forty times a year in smoke-filled arenas.

Where Shakur’s comparison falls completely flat is what Leonard actually did when boxing finesse failed. When Leonard got pulled into absolute hell against Roberto Duran in Montreal, he stood flat-footed and fought. When he was fading and behind on the cards against Thomas Hearns, he unleashed a vicious, predatory assault to close the show. Leonard had a ruthless finishing instinct.

Shakur takes the defensive, perimeter-oriented parts of Leonard’s style and strips away the violent bite. Robinson was a destructive puncher who could knock an opponent out going backward or forward. Shakur is a pure points collector who treats contact like a disaster.

Shakur looking at Robinson and favoring Leonard sounds like modern revisionism. It is a fighter who relies on safety and low output, trying to validate his own approach, overlooking the fact that both Sugar Rays had an appetite for destruction that Shakur has never shown inside a ring.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia May Vacate Rather Than Fight Bektemir Melikuziev
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia may give up his WBA super middleweight title rather than defend it against Bektemir Melikuziev. Rick Glaser says Munguia’s team is considering that option. If his information is right, the decision would fit a career that has generally been managed with care. I expected Munguia’s team to have little appetite for Bek once the mandatory fight was ordered.

Glaser says Munguia’s camp is taking a “deep dive into the idea of giving up the title.” He has not said Munguia has vacated. The WBA has given the two sides until October 21 to make a deal and may call a purse bid if they fail to agree.

The Golden Boy connection makes this especially revealing. Melikuziev has fought under its banner since turning professional, and the company knows what its own fighter would bring against Munguia. Bek is a powerful southpaw with a damaging body attack. Munguia’s willingness to take punches while pressing forward would give him chances to land, but it would also give Bek chances to hurt him.

Munguia (46-2, 35 KOs) accepted the Canelo Alvarez fight for a huge payday and lost. Bruno Surace then knocked him out in a matchup Munguia was favored to win. Sergiy Derevyanchenko gave Munguia a hard fight, so his record is not free of risk. Melikuziev presents a different calculation: considerable danger with nowhere near Canelo’s commercial reward.

The WBA belt helped Munguia regain world champion status when he beat José Armando Reséndiz in May. Defending it is another matter. A purse bid could also take the choice of date, venue, and broadcaster out of his team’s hands. Vacating would leave Munguia free to pursue a bigger name at 168, though that freedom would come at Bek’s expense.

Melikuziev (17-1, 11 KOs) beat Darius Fulghum in a WBA eliminator in May 2025, then watched Munguia get the fight with Reséndiz. Bek told The Ring he had been assured he would get the next shot. If Munguia vacates, Bek may still get a chance to win the belt. He would lose the chance to win it from Munguia, a victory that would mean far more for his career.

We’re seeing the new age of belt-holders. Champions giving up their belts exposes the entire modern hustle around world titles. Fighters treat sanctioning body belts like disposable leverage tools rather than something to defend against legitimate threats. They want the belt purely to slap “world champion” on a poster, collect the promotional bump, and leverage it into an in-house payday.

The second a dangerous, low-profile puncher gets ordered as a mandatory, they drop the trinket in the trash and run. Look at the pattern playing out right now. Hamzah Sheeraz walked away from his belt rather than get in the ring with Janibek Alimkhanuly. Teofimo Lopez is on the verge of playing the same game,

Now Jaime Munguia’s camp looks ready to dump the WBA strap because Bektemir Melikuziev offers pure risk with zero casual crossover appeal. Bektemir is a nightmare matchup for a flawed fighter like Munguia. Bek is a heavy-handed, compact southpaw who specializes in cracking the ribs and punishing guys who march forward without defense.

Against Bektemir, Munguia risks getting stopped on regular DAZN for modest money, completely torpedoing his marketability for another mega-fight. Dumping the title completely strips away the pretense of championship prestige. Decades ago, winning a belt meant you took on whoever climbed the ladder, regardless of style or reward. What we’re seeing now is champions treating mandatory defenses like bad business propositions.

If Munguia vacates, Bektemir Melikuziev should get the first chance at the vacant WBA title, but the WBA would still have to choose his opponent. Its current rankings put Canelo Alvarez at No. 2 and José Armando Reséndiz at No. 3. A Canelo fight would be the biggest prize for Bek, though there is no indication Canelo wants it.

Reséndiz looks like the more realistic choice: he lost the belt to Munguia in May and would have a chance to win it back. That would give Bek a title opportunity, but it would deny him the higher-profile victory over Munguia that he has spent more than a year pursuing.

Sports.title: Cuban Boxing Greatness Crossed a Dividing Line
Sports.content:
Cuba produced professional stars before it became an Olympic boxing power. That history makes any list of its greatest fighters difficult to rank. Kid Chocolate and Kid Gavilan built their names in long professional careers; Teófilo Stevenson and Félix Savón never fought professionally. The dividing line was a political decision in 1962 that changed what a Cuban boxer could do with his talent.

Chocolate was a major New York attraction in the 1930s, admired for his speed and two-handed punching. Gavilan later won the welterweight title and made the bolo punch his signature. Luis Rodriguez added another championship to Cuba’s professional history when he beat Emile Griffith for the welterweight title in 1963. These men built their reputations in fights against the leading professionals of their day.

After Cuba banned professional boxing, a fighter who wanted that career had to pursue it abroad. José Nápoles became a welterweight champion after making his home in Mexico. José Legrá won the featherweight title while based in Spain. Later fighters such as Erislandy Lara left Cuba to compete for professional titles. Their success carried a personal cost that a list of wins and belts cannot show.

Cuba also built an amateur program under coach Alcides Sagarra that produced generations of Olympic champions. Stevenson won heavyweight gold in 1972, 1976 and 1980. Savón won the same prize in 1992, 1996 and 2000. Their medals need no imagined professional careers to give them value. But the absence of professional fights leaves one question open: how would the system’s best have performed against established champions over twelve rounds?

Guillermo Rigondeaux gave that question a partial answer. He won Olympic gold in 2000 and 2004, then left Cuba and became a professional champion. In 2013, he beat Nonito Donaire in a super bantamweight title fight, controlling distance and making a dangerous puncher miss repeatedly. Donaire was a proven champion, and Rigondeaux’s amateur schooling held up against him. One fight cannot settle how Stevenson or Savón would have fared as professionals, but it gives this comparison something firmer than speculation.

Lara’s December 2025 defense of the WBA middleweight title shows that Cuban fighters still succeed on the professional side of that divide. The strongest case for Cuba’s boxing greatness comes from looking at both sides: champions who proved themselves over long professional careers, Olympic greats whose careers took another course, and Rigondeaux, who crossed between them and beat one of the best.

Ghana News.title: Hundreds of thousands expected in Paris for Pope’s visit
Ghana News.content:
Paris visit for Pope

Pope Leo XIV embarks on a four-day visit to France on Friday, with the highpoint being a giant Mass attended by more than half a million people in central Paris.

For Saturday's afternoon celebration, an altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde, and police have sealed off a large area around the Champs-Élysées.

Some 600,000 Catholic faithful are expected to cram the avenue up to the Arc de Triomphe and beyond.

Large crowds are also expected at other stages of the Pope's itinerary, reflecting an enthusiasm the Church attributes to growing spiritual thirst among the French and other Europeans.

President Emmanuel Macron will greet the Pope at Orly airport on Friday morning, and then hold talks with him at the Élysée Palace on geopolitical issues and artificial intelligence (AI). He will also deliver a speech with the Pope in Metz.

However, the president will not be at any of the Pope's Masses, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.

Instead, his wife Brigitte and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will attend the Champs-Élysées Mass. Several candidates for next year's presidential election are also due, including Marine Le Pen of the nationalist right, centrists Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal, and conservative Bruno Retailleau.

There were reports of tensions between Macron and the Vatican team sent to make arrangements, with the president allegedly frustrated in his wish for a more ceremonial aspect to the visit.

This was dismissed this week by Élysée officials, who said it was customary to offer a visiting head of state – which the Pope is – a range of high-profile events, such as a cavalry escort down the Champs-Élysées. But they said they never expected the Pope to take the offer up.

They did confirm that Pope Leo turned down Macron's idea of a meeting with artisans who helped rebuild the fire-devastated Notre-Dame cathedral. They said his agenda was too tight.

After a Popemobile ride through crowds to Notre-Dame Cathedral on Friday afternoon, Pope Leo XIV will be joined in the evening by 80,000 young people at the Stade de France in northern Paris.

On Sunday 150,000 have signed up to attend mass in the Pyrenean sanctuary of Lourdes.

Preparations are taking place in Lourdes ahead of the visit

On Monday the Pope will be in Metz, in northeast France, where he will pay tribute to Robert Schuman (1886-1963), a founding father of the European Union and a fervent Catholic who is today a candidate for beatification.

The Pope will also meet a group of migrants in Paris, and in Lourdes some victims of sexual abuse by members of the Catholic clergy.

Born in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV was originally called Robert Prevost – a French name.

In fact his paternal grandmother was born in Le Havre in Normandy in 1894. When she married in the US many years later, she and her Italian husband took the name Prevost, her mother's maiden name.

France has a historically complex relationship with the Catholic Church of Rome. The country was long known as the "Eldest Daughter of the Church" because, supposedly but inaccurately, it was the first kingdom to convert to Christianity. Actually, Armenia, Georgia and Ethiopia preceded it.

In the 14th century, the papacy came into exile in Avignon in southern France, and over the following centuries French armies periodically intervened in Italian politics, where popes were secular rulers as well as heads of the Church.

Napoleon held two popes in captivity.

Recent popes have all come to France, most notably John-Paul II, who came several times between 1980 and 2004, and Pope Francis who came three times, but avoided Paris, going instead to Strasbourg, Marseilles and Corsica.

Pope John Paul II, pictured here in Paris in 1980, visited many times

Today France has secularised with the rest of Europe, and less than half of the population identifies as Catholic.

The number of regular worshippers has fallen from 35% of the population in 1960 to less than 5% today, while the number of priests has shrunk by two-thirds from 25,000 in 1990 to fewer than 9,000.

But in recent years there have been signs of a growing interest in religious tradition, with the number of adult baptisms more than doubling in five years to hit 10,000 in 2025.

"France has indeed secularised, but there is a void where God and values used to be," said Cardinal François Bustillo, Bishop of Ajaccio.

"People are searching for something. Maybe they go to India or Tibet or the Amazon. And now the Pope comes here from Rome, bringing a reminder to people of their own roots.

"It was John-Paul II who awoke the East. Now Leo XIV will awake the West," he said.

Ghana News.title: Abena Kyei Boakye unveiled as Ambassador for Glow Washing Powder
Ghana News.content:
Award-winning TV personality Abena Kyei Boakye has been unveiled as the new brand ambassador for Glow Washing Powder, a Ghanaian-owned detergent brand. The unveiling ceremony was held at the ESP Hotel in Labone, Accra, on Thursday evening.

Glow Washing Powder is positioned as an effective laundry solution designed to remove stubborn stains without prolonged soaking or excessive scrubbing.

It is marketed as tough on dirt while being gentle on clothes, making it suitable for everyday clothing, workwear and school uniforms.

Speaking on behalf of the CEO of Glow Soaps & Detergents, Nana Akua Darkowaa, also known as Faustina Darko, Madam Sweetie Acquah said the company is committed to providing effective and affordable cleaning products while building a strong Ghanaian brand.

She said Abena’s appointment would help increase awareness of Glow Washing Powder and take the product closer to consumers across the country. Glow Soaps & Detergents is a Ghanaian-owned company that manufactures a range of household and commercial cleaning products, including bar soap, liquid soap, bleach, floor cleaner, glass cleaner, sanitiser and disinfectants. The company has been expanding its distribution network through retailers, direct sales and market activations.

Presidential Adviser and Director of Diaspora Affairs at the Office of the President, Kofi Okyere Darko (KOD), who performed the official unveiling, said the strongest brand partnerships are built when an individual’s personality, values and audience align with what the brand represents. “The strongest partnerships happen when an individual's personality, values, and audience connect naturally with what the brand represents.

And I believe that is exactly what we're seeing this evening,” he said. He lauded Abena for building a strong, relatable, and engaging presence in the Ghanaian media space. “Those qualities make her a wonderful partner for Glow Washing Powder, a brand that is going to be part of every Ghanaian home,” KOD said, adding that the partnership celebrates the modern Ghanaian woman. “This partnership is also about celebrating the modern Ghanaian woman: versatile, confident, hardworking, vibrant, and always finding ways to make life better for herself and her family.

Abena represents many of those qualities. ”So this evening, we don't just sign a contract; we celebrate a partnership, a new chapter, and possibilities that come with it. Abena, welcome to the Glow family, and let's make it clean, fresh, and unforgettable,” he added.

In her acceptance speech, Abena Kyei Boakye said the partnership was more than an endorsement. “It is a pleasure to be here with you this evening. Indeed, today is more than an unveiling for me. It is the beginning of a beautiful partnership with a brand that understands something very important, when you look good, feel good, and live clean, you glow differently,” she said. “For me, Glow is not just about washing clothes.

It is about freshness, confidence and that beautiful feeling you get when your clothes are clean, bright and ready for the world. “She pledged to bring the Glow experience closer to consumers. “So, whether you are washing for yourself, your children or the whole family, remember one thing: Wash with Glow. Wear your confidence. And let yourself glow! “The ceremony was emceed by Joy Prime presenter Kpekpo Maxwell Justice (KMJ) and featured a comedy performance by Comedian Hogan. In attendance were Gospel musician Nacee, Counsellor George Lutterodt, and Ghana’s Most Beautiful personality Belinda Fosua Amoah, popularly known as Fosua, among other guests.

Ghana News.title: Côte d’Ivoire 2-0 Ghana: Sibo earns lowest mark as Boakye takes opportunity – Black Stars ratings
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s quest to return to the Africa Cup of Nations got off to a false start after losing 2-0 to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké in their opening game of the 2027 edition qualifiers.

A first-half strike by Malick Yalcouyé and a Franck Kessié spot kick in the second were the difference, with the Elephants getting an important win, while it looks like déjà vu for the Black Stars, who begin another AFCON qualifying cycle with a defeat.

Here’s how each Ghana player was rated in the game out of ten, with ten being the highest mark.

Lawrence Ati Zigi – 3

The St. Gallen goalkeeper was not the busiest man on the pitch, especially in the first half, but when his first real test arrived, he was caught off guard by the Malick Yalcouyé goal. The goal can’t be entirely pinned on him because the two midfielders allowed the Brighton man to shoot instead of pressing him.

Kojo Oppong Peprah – 2

The 22-year-old was played out of position at right-back and was found wanting a lot of the time when he came up against Yan Diomande. He couldn’t move the ball up and struggled to pick out teammates with his passes. Peprah didn’t also get enough help from Fatawu, but his lack of fitness, having played just 21 minutes this season, showed.

Gideon Mensah – 3

His first half was particularly not great, with the ball stuck under his feet a number of times, but the FC Köln full-back improved in the second half.

Alexander Djiku – 5

The captain on the day was decent and came out on top in most of the defensive actions the Spartak Moscow central defender was involved in.

Jerome Opoku – 5

Like his centre-back pairing, there were not many questions about his contribution to the game. The Istanbul Basaksehir man was particularly successful with his duels.

Fatawu Issahaku – 3

The Ipswich winger was isolated for a lot of the game, also because he was paired with a centre-back-turned-full-back in Peprah. When he had the ball, he ran into no man’s land and lost possession – zero end product coming from the situations he was involved in. Fatawu was unlucky to concede a penalty that would likely not be given if there was VAR.

Kwasi Sibo – 2

The Al-Swehly midfielder was involved in the most defining moment in the game – the Yalcouyé goal – where he was caught ball-watching when he should have been pressing. He couldn’t provide the protection to the backline that he was supposed to bring, lacked passing quality and, as usual, struggled to pick out teammates with his passes.

Caleb Yirenkyi – 2

The Coventry man, just like his midfield partner, probably let the team down by not pressing or closing down Yalcouyé for the Côte d’Ivoire opener. He played like a man lacking confidence and was jittery with a lot of his actions.

Christopher Baah Bonsu – 4

The Al Qadsiah winger had a bright start to the game and caused the Ivorians a lot of problems down the left, creating half-chances for the team before the Côte d’Ivoire goal turned the tide.

Ernest Nuamah – 5

Though a lot of his runs finished at a dead end, the Lyon winger was Ghana’s most dangerous man until he was taken off. He would have been more useful if deployed on either wing with a natural striker receiving his services.

Brandon Thomas-Asante – 3

The Coventry attacker was isolated for a lot of the time he was on the pitch and was required to do too much running by being at both ends of the pitch at all times, and ended up doing very little.

Substitutes

Augustine Boakye – 4

The St. Etienne attacking midfielder, in 26 minutes, showed why Ghanaians screamed for him to be involved throughout the World Cup period and made the moment count when it came. The 25-year-old was always eager to get the ball forward since his introduction and generated a lot of promising situations during his time on the pitch.

Benjamin Tetteh – 4

Probably should have scored towards the end but showed why the team needs a target man with the amount of attention and action he drew in his 26 minutes on the pitch.

Felix Afena-Gyan – 3

The Igdir forward had no excuse not to find the back of the net but instead acted as a defender for Côte d’Ivoire, heading the ball out off the post when he should have been heading it in.

Jonas Adjetey – 3

Got 19 minutes, a period when Ghana was probably on top of the game.

Ibrahim Sulemana – 3

The Sassuolo midfielder didn’t have a lot of time to affect the game, just like Gyan, and was the extra body the team perhaps needed in midfield from the start.

Carlos Queiroz - Head coach – 3

With the materials at his disposal, Queiroz coached a goalless draw but left himself short by playing just two midfielders from the start.

Ghana News.title: Stance considering autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty ‘could constitute most feasible solution’
Ghana News.content:
Jamaica’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, Kamina Johnson Smith, welcomed on Wednesday in New York the adoption of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2797.

This expresses full support for the UN Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy in facilitating and conducting negotiations, taking as a basis Morocco’s Autonomy Plan, and affirming that genuine autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty could constitute a most feasible solution.

This position was expressed in a joint communiqué signed by Johnson Smith and Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccan Expatriates, Nasser Bourita.

It follows talks held on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The communiqué congratulates the Kingdom of Morocco on its diplomatic efforts to secure international consensus and momentum in favor of the Autonomy Plan, under the leadership of King Mohammed VI.

During their talks, Nasser Bourita and Johnson Smith agreed to continue political consultations between the Kingdom of Morocco and Jamaica and to coordinate their positions on issues of common interest.

Ghana News.title: Blaming cocaine problem on NACOC’s removal from ports is absurd – Amankwa-Manu
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Defence and Interior Committee, Kofi Amankwa-Manu, has dismissed claims that Ghana’s current cocaine trafficking problem is linked to the removal of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) from the country’s list of Port Inspection Agencies in 2018.

He described the argument as “absurd”, insisting that Ghana’s recent drug-related challenges point to broader security gaps that require urgent attention.

His comments follow remarks by GoldBod Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, that the removal of NACOC from the list of Port Inspection Agencies in June 2018 weakened Ghana’s capacity to detect and prevent drug trafficking through its ports.

Mr Gyamfi argued that the decision undermined NACOC’s port inspection role despite the Commission’s mandate to monitor, regulate and enforce laws relating to narcotics trafficking.

But speaking on Joy FM’s Newsnight, Mr Amankwa-Manu rejected the attempt to link the current situation to the 2018 decision.

“Within 18 months, we have this situation, and then we are saying that because NACOC was taken from the ports in 2018, that is why we have this problem? For me, that is absurd. It is absurd, and we cannot go that angle,” he said.

He said the concerns raised by the Interior Minister about elements operating in Ghana, and intelligence agencies’ reluctance to share information with the country, indicate more serious security challenges that must be addressed.

“If your Interior Minister, who has oversight responsibility, tells you that we have elements in this country who are behind this, that there is a problem. If your Interior Minister, who has oversight responsibility, tells you that even intelligence agencies do not trust Ghana to the extent of refusing to share intelligence, then there is a problem,” he said.

Mr Amankwa-Manu maintained that the focus should be on identifying and closing the security gaps rather than on assigning blame for a decision made years ago.

He further argued that Parliament can address the concerns through a bipartisan approach, stressing that national security should take precedence over partisan considerations.

“It is Ghana we are building. We are not building NDC. We are not building NPP. We are building Ghana,” he said.

Mr Amankwa-Manu said the same bipartisan approach is adopted when the Defence and Interior Committee considers security matters and questioned why Parliament could not apply it to the current cocaine-related concerns.

Ghana News.title: AFCON 2027Q: Black Stars open campaign with defeat to Ivory Coast in Bouaké
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's hopes of making a winning start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign suffered a setback as the Black Stars lost 2-0 to Ivory Coast in Bouaké

Malick Yalcouye opened the scoring with a powerful strike from outside the box before Frank Kessie doubled the hosts' advantage from the penalty spot in the second half.

The defeat leaves Ghana at the bottom of Group C ahead of Friday's meeting between The Gambia and Somalia.

Ghana came into the game looking to return to the continental showpiece after missing the previous Africa Cup of Nations for the first time in 20 years.

However, Carlos Queiroz's side struggled to create clear opportunities against an Ivory Coast team that controlled much of the match.

The Black Stars were without several key players because of injuries, including captain Jordan Ayew, Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo, Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus and Thomas Partey.

Brandon Thomas was tasked with leading the attack, with Christopher Bonsu Baah and Fatawu Issahaku operating alongside him and Ernest Nuamah playing behind the centre-forward.

Ghana created little during the opening stages, although Nuamah came close to giving the visitors a breakthrough midway through the first half.

The forward noticed the Ivory Coast goalkeeper off his line and attempted a long-range effort in the 20th minute, but his shot drifted wide.

The hosts eventually broke the deadlock in the 29th minute as Yalcouye produced a powerful effort from just outside the box into the bottom-right corner.

The scorer attacked down the left side of the penalty area and went to ground following a challenge from Fatawu.

The referee pointed to the spot, with Ghanaian players protesting the decision. After a lengthy delay, Kessie stepped up and converted from 12 yards in the 56th minute.

By that stage, Ghana had still failed to register a shot on target and had conceded 62% of possession to their opponents.

Queiroz responded with a triple substitution in the 64th minute.

Felix Afena-Gyan, Benjamin Tetteh and Augustine Boakye were introduced, replacing Nuamah, Brandon Asante and Christopher Bonsu Baah.

The changes brought some attacking urgency from Ghana, but the Black Stars were unable to find a way back into the contest.

It took until nearly the 80th minute for Ghana to register their first efforts on target, with Benjamin Tetteh and Caleb Yirenkyi testing the Ivory Coast defence.

Afena-Gyan and Augustine Boakye, who was making his long-awaited Black Stars debut, came close to reducing the deficit in stoppage time.

Ghana will now regroup as they look ahead to their next Group C fixture against The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium on September 29.

Ghana News.title: From construction site to top of class: Daniel Doe emerges Legon’s best Computer Engineering student
Ghana News.content:
Daniel Agudey Doe

Daniel Agudey Doe, a Computer Engineering graduate of the University of Ghana, has emerged as the best graduating student in his programme after navigating significant financial difficulties during his university education.

Before receiving financial assistance through the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship, Daniel worked on construction sites and took on other manual labour jobs during vacations to raise money for tuition and living expenses.

His financial challenges also affected his ability to meet basic needs on campus, with occasions when he had to skip meals.

“I was simply trying to make it through university. If things became impossible and I had to drop out, at least I could say I had given university my best attempt,” he said.

Daniel entered the University of Ghana with an interest in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning and hoped to eventually build a career in Robotics.

However, the financial demands of university meant that completing his degree was uncertain.

Scholarship eased financial pressure

That changed after he was selected as a beneficiary of the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship.

The scholarship covered his tuition and hostel fees and provided additional support for his studies.

Daniel said the assistance allowed him to devote more attention to his academic work without having to spend his vacations primarily looking for money to return to school.

“For the first time, I had the privilege many financially stable students have, the ability to focus on my studies without constantly worrying about tuition, hostel fees, or survival,” he said.

With the financial pressure reduced, Daniel said he was able to participate more actively in group studies and devote more time to his coursework.

He eventually graduated as the Best Graduating Computer Engineering Student at the University of Ghana.

Daniel believes the financial support was critical to his completing the programme.

“Without the scholarship, I genuinely do not believe I would have completed university. I may have dropped out as early as Level 200 due to financial pressure,” he said.

From construction to technology

Daniel is currently undertaking his National Service at Amalitech as a Data Engineer.

He intends to build experience in data engineering before moving into Machine Learning and, eventually, Robotics.

He is also considering pursuing a master’s degree in Robotics or a related field combining Robotics and Artificial Intelligence.

Daniel said guidance from his scholarship coordinator, Mr George, also helped him consider his options ahead of his National Service placement.

Scholarship programme

Daniel is among students supported under the MTN Ghana Foundation’s Bright Scholarship programme, which was introduced in 2017.

According to information provided by the foundation, the programme has supported 1,220 students in tertiary institutions across Ghana.

The scholarship covers tuition and accommodation and includes support for a laptop, books and study materials.

The programme has also recorded several academic distinctions among its beneficiaries, with 17 scholars graduating as valedictorians or best students at their institutions and 299 graduating with first-class honours.

For Daniel, his journey from working on construction sites to graduating at the top of his Computer Engineering class demonstrates the difference financial support can make for students facing difficulties in funding their education.

“The MTN Bright Scholarship did not just change my life; it positively impacted my family and my community,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Mahama: Peaceful political transitions prove democracy can work in Africa
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama has pointed to Ghana’s record of peaceful political transitions as evidence that democratic institutions can provide a stable framework for managing changes in political leadership.

Addressing world leaders at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, President Mahama said Ghana had remained committed to constitutional democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights.

“Ghana is arguably the most stable democracy in Africa,” he said, adding that the country was determined to demonstrate that “democracy works”.

President Mahama said Ghana’s democratic system allows political differences to be resolved through constitutional processes, participation and consensus rather than through force or instability.

He acknowledged that democratic systems can sometimes be slower in taking decisions because they require consultation and adherence to constitutional procedures. However, he said those processes help create decisions that are more sustainable because they are rooted in participation and legitimacy.

The President said Ghana’s experience was also relevant to the broader African debate on democratic governance, particularly the need for political systems to deliver meaningful improvements in citizens’ lives.

He maintained that democracy should ultimately produce tangible social and economic benefits, including access to education, healthcare, housing, food and economic opportunity, alongside the protection of political and civil rights.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
