Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has expressed his horror at an “evil” knife attack carried out today by a Ukrainian man at a Catholic abbey in Poland, which left one priest dead and others seriously injured. The incident has caused shock in Poland, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk pledging that the perpetrator, who is in police custody, will face the “full severity of Polish law”. W Opactwie Sióstr Benedyktynek w Jarosławiu obywatel Ukrainy dopuścił się straszliwej zbrodni. Jesteśmy wstrząśnięci tym złem. Według dotychczasowych informacji zginął ksiądz katolicki, a kilka innych osób zostało rannych. Składamy najgłębsze kondolencje rodzinie i bliskim… — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) September 24, 2026 The attack took place on Thursday morning on the grounds of a Benedictine abbey in the town of Jarosław in southeast Poland. Local police reported that a 31-year-old Ukrainian man had stabbed four male victims and one female. Three were members of the clergy and two laypeople. Authorities later confirmed that one of the men, a priest, had died of his injuries in hospital and that two others were in serious condition. The cathedral in the nearby city of Rzeszów named the deceased as Stanisław Zbojnowicz. The superior of the Benedictine Sisters Monastery, Barbara Dendor, told news website Interia that Zbojnowicz had been in a confessional when the attack began. He had rushed out to attempt to close the gates and protect other people, but was stabbed by the assailant before he could do so. In its initial social media post announcing Zbojnowicz’s death, the cathedral also said that a second priest, Marek Pieńkowski, had died. However, a few minutes later it deleted that claim, blaming the “enormous information chaos surrounding today’s tragic event”. One person was killed and four were injured in a knife attack at a Catholic convent in Poland this morning, with clergy among the victims. Police have detained a 31-year-old Ukrainian man on suspicion of carrying out the attack. The motive remains unknown https://t.co/93nbqpwnIA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 24, 2026 On Thursday afternoon, prosecutors revealed that the suspect, who has not been named, had entered Poland from Germany in the early hours of Thursday and “was heading to the border crossing [with Ukraine] in Korczowa”, which is around 30km (18.6 miles) from Jarosław. However, he ultimately did not cross the border and, for unknown reasons, ended up in Jarosław, where he entered the grounds of the abbey and began his attack, using a knife taken from the kitchen. Prosecutors said that doctors would assess the suspect’s condition before he was interrogated. Blood samples were also taken to be tested for the presence of narcotics and alcohol. The motive for the attack remains unknown. Dendor told news website Wirtualna Polska that the perpetrator was unknown to them. “He looked like a madman, in shorts and a T-shirt, even though it was cold today,” she said. Wirtualna Polska reports, based on the accounts of unnamed witnesses, that the Ukrainian man had earlier in the day knocked on the gates of the abbey and asked for financial assistance. However, he was turned away due to the suspicion that he was drunk or under the influence of drugs and was asked to come back later. That is standard practice for places that offer aid, reports the news service. The man “flew into a rage when he didn’t get help and allegedly threatened priests”, said one of the unnamed sources. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk expressed his sympathy for the loved ones of the victims of the attack and pledged that the perpetrator “will be punished with the full severity of Polish law”. President Karol Nawrocki likewise expressed his condolences and called on the authorities to “quickly and thoroughly clarify all the circumstances of this tragedy”. Later on Thursday afternoon, Zelensky also extended his condolences in a social media post published in Polish. “We are shocked by this evil,” he wrote. “The perpetrator of this evil must bear full responsibility in accordance with the applicable law.” Morderca z Jarosławia jest w rękach Polskiej Policji. Trwają czynności. Sprawca to obywatel Ukrainy. Będzie ukarany z całą surowością polskiego prawa. Łączę się w bólu z bliskimi ofiar tego brutalnego ataku. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) September 24, 2026 Earlier, the Ukrainian embassy in Warsaw had “condemned the brutal attack” in Jarosław. However, it also appealed for people “not to allow pain to turn into hatred or further violence”, saying that “accountability for the crime must be based solely on the law”. Polish-Ukrainian relations have been tense in recent months, amid rising anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland and anger at Zelensky’s decision to name a military unit after a group that led massacres of Poles during World War Two. There has been a rise in reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland this year. Marcin Piotrowski, a board member of the Folkowisko Foundation, which provides aid to Ukrainian refugees, told newspaper Rzeczpospolita today that the tragedy in Jarosław was already being exploited on social media. World.title: Polish constitutional court officials charged with preventing entry of new judges
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The crisis around Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has deepened further, after prosecutors charged two senior TK officials over their role in preventing new judges from taking up their positions on the court. Those judges were chosen by the government’s majority in parliament but rejected by President Karol Nawrocki and the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, both of whom are aligned with the right-wing opposition. Following news of the charges, Święczkowski announced that he has initiated proceedings of his own against three other new judges who were admitted to the court this year after being chosen by the ruling coalition. That could result in them being expelled from their positions. Zarzuty w śledztwie dotyczącym niedopuszczenia sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego do orzekania: ⬇️https://t.co/MPiKCEqGBs — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) September 23, 2026 After coming to power in December 2023, the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk refused to recognise the TK, which was stacked with judges appointed by the former Law and Justice administration. It argued that, because some of those judges were unlawfully appointed, the TK itself was illegitimate. Earlier this year, Tusk’s majority in parliament finally began the process of appointing new judges to the TK to fill the growing number of vacancies. Normally, 15 judges sit on the tribunal, but many seats were empty after incumbents’ nine-year terms had expired and the government had previously refused to fill them. However, under Polish law, new TK judges must take an oath “before the president” in order to take up their position. Nawrocki, who was elected last year with the support of PiS, has refused to swear in four of the six judges chosen by parliament in March. Nawrocki argues that there were legal doubts surrounding their election. The government rejects this, as do the judges themselves, who organised their own swearing-in ceremony before a notary and then submitted the documents to the presidential chancellery. Afterwards, the four judges attempted to take up their positions at the TK. However, Święczkowski, who served in the PiS government before becoming a TK judge, refused to admit them, arguing that they had not taken the necessary oath before the president. The judges took their case to the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), which in May issued an interim order requiring that they be allowed to take up their positions. But Święczkowski has refused to comply, arguing that the ECHR does not have the competence to make such a decision. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 While Święczkowski himself is protected from prosecution by legal immunity, two senior TK officials have now been charged over their role in refusing entry to the four judges. One of the two suspects, who can be named only as Zofia H. under Polish privacy law, is the director of the TK’s chancellery; the other, Piotr P., is the commander of the TK’s security service. They have been charged with abuse of power by a public official, which is punishable by up to three years in prison, and “maliciously and persistently” violating the employment rights of the judges, an offence that carries a sentence of up to two years. Prosecutors say that the officials’ actions were “to the detriment of the private interests of judges of the Constitutional Tribunal and the public interest in the proper functioning of the judiciary in Poland”. Both of the accused have been questioned and pleaded not guilty. The crisis around Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has deepened further after the tribunal ruled that the president is not obliged to swear in new TK judges appointed by parliament. President Nawrocki last month refused to swear in four new judges https://t.co/ycnweW9pSR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 13, 2026 The decision to bring charges was welcomed by Waldemar Żurek, who serves as justice minister in Tusk’s government as well as prosecutor general. “In a building that should stand guard over the constitution, unlawful blockades were organised, humiliating inspections were conducted, and malicious bullying was directed at legally elected judges,” he wrote on social media. “A state official has no right to place themselves above the law, and the gates of the tribunal are not the gates of a private fortress,” he continued. “Anyone who carries out unlawful political orders and destroys the foundations of the rule of law must reckon with criminal liability.” W budynku, który powinien stać na straży Konstytucji, urządzono bezprawne blokady, upokarzające kontrole i złośliwy mobbing wobec legalnie wybranych sędziów. Urzędnik państwowy nie ma prawa stawiać się ponad prawem, a bramy Trybunału nie są bramami prywatnej twierdzy.… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) September 23, 2026 The TK itself, however, condemned prosecutors’ actions, calling them “unlawful” and a “tool of personal pressure and a form of intimidation”. “The director of the chancellery and all other employees of the TK have performed and continue to perform their duties and official orders in accordance with the applicable law,” wrote the tribunal on its official X account. It argued that it would, in fact, have been a criminal abuse of power to have “allowed persons who have not taken the oath before the President to assume the office of a TK judge”. W dniu dzisiejszym @PK_GOV_PL przedstawiła Pani Dyrektor Kancelarii Trybunału Konstytucyjnego absurdalne zarzuty z art. 231 § 1 i 218 § 3 Kodeksu karnego, które od początku do końca są oparte na wymyślonych podstawach prawnych. Działanie to stanowi kolejną próbę wywarcia wpływu… — Trybunał Konstytucyjny (@TK_GOV_PL) September 23, 2026 On Thursday, the day after the charges were announced, the TK issued a further statement saying that Święczkowski had initiated proceedings against three new TK judges who were chosen by parliament this year and sworn in by Nawrocki (two in March, the other in June). The TK said that it was assessing complaints that two of those judges filed against tribunal employees, as well as their refusal to participate in sessions of the TK’s general assembly. Those three judges have shown solidarity with their four excluded colleagues by refusing to participate. “These proceedings may conclude with the most severe ruling of the disciplinary court in the form of removal from office of the aforementioned TK judges,” wrote the TK. Prezes @TK_GOV_PL Bogdan Święczkowski, działając na wniosek jednego z sędziów, wszczął dzisiaj postępowanie mogące się zakończyć zarzutami dyscyplinarnymi wobec trojga sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego: Magdaleny Bentkowskiej, Dariusza Szostka oraz Sławomira Patyry.… — Trybunał Konstytucyjny (@TK_GOV_PL) September 24, 2026 An eighth new TK judge chosen this year, Maciej Berek, who was elected by parliament earlier this month, has also not yet been sworn in by Nawrocki. Berek’s appointment has been particularly controversial, given that he served in the government until being nominated to the TK. Tusk described Berek as his “right-hand man”. Even some MPs from Tusk’s ruling coalition voted against Berek’s appointment, arguing that it contradicted the government’s own efforts to “depoliticise” the judiciary, including by banning recently serving politicians from sitting on the TK. The presidential chancellery has so far refused to swear in Berek based on a technicality, arguing that there is no evidence he has previously served for at least ten years as a legal counsel, which is a requirement to sit on the TK. Berek says that he has presented such evidence. A fire last night at a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company, was caused deliberately, says digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski. The facility is used to provide internet services across the region, including in Ukraine, which relies heavily on Starlink connections. Although the fire is still being investigated, “the modus operandi in this case is clearly Russian”, says Gawkowski. 🔴 Gawkowski o pożarze stacji Starlink. "Element wojny hybrydowej" Wicepremier Krzysztof Gawkowski ocenił pożar stacji Starlink na Mazowszu jako celową próbę zakłócenia łączności. – Wiele wskazuje na to, że pożar stacji Starlinków na Mazowszu to kolejny element wojny hybrydowej… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) September 24, 2026 Firefighters were called out at around 9 p.m. on Wednesday to the facility, which is located in the village of Wola Krobowska, just south of the capital Warsaw. Due to suspicions that the fire had been caused deliberately, police and officers from the Internal Security Agency (ABW) were also later dispatched to the scene. “We’re dealing with an arson attack that was intended to impact critical telecommunications infrastructure that influences internet operation,” Gawkowski, who also serves as deputy prime minister, told broadcaster TVN on Thursday morning. In a separate interview with TVP, the minister said that the facility is owned by Polish state telecommunications operator Exatel and “provides internet transmission through Poland, and also to Ukraine”. He noted that other internet providers use Exatel’s facility, including Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which is the owner of Starlink. Starlink terminals have been vital in Ukraine during Russia’s war against the country. Gawkowski told TVN that “the modus operandi in this case is clearly Russian” and “is another element of the hybrid warfare we are facing”. Poland has been one of the primary targets for Russian sabotage operations in Europe, including a series of arson attacks. “The Russians want to paralyse critical infrastructure, cut off water, gas and electricity, paralyse the internet,” said the minister. “All these processes have one goal: to incite panic and stir up emotions.” However, in his remarks to TVP, Gawkowski acknowledged that, for now, “it is impossible to say” for sure whether Russia was behind the attack. Poland is the "primary focus" of Russia's sabotage campaign in Europe, finds a new report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism. Among 151 incidents identified since 2022, 31 of them took place in Poland – more than in any other country https://t.co/QXfSI00FD6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 3, 2026 The spokesman for Poland’s security services, Jacek Dobrzyński, likewise told TVN that “at this stage it is still too early to talk about the causes or motives of this fire”. However, he confirmed that “everything points to arson”. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek also told broadcaster RMF that “this could be an act of sabotage, and we are taking that into account, so nothing can be ruled out here, especially since these are sensitive elements that ensure satellite communications”. Polish news service Defence24 notes that ground stations are used by Starlink to connect its satellite constellation with terrestrial communications infrastructure. The facility in Poland, alongside one in Lithuania, serves the entire Central and Eastern Europe region, including Ukraine. Tu nieco więcej o roli stacji naziemnych w systemie Starlink. https://t.co/EYys481dSi — Mariusz Marszałkowski (@MJMarszalkowski) September 24, 2026 Earlier this month, a fire broke out at a drone plant in Poland belonging to WB Electronics, which supplies the armed forces of Ukraine and Poland, among others. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that there was “no doubt” the fire was caused deliberately, and that Russia was likely behind it. The Polish government has in recent months warned that Russia is planning to escalate its hybrid actions against Poland and other countries in the region, including through acts of sabotage, disinformation, and potential airspace and border violations. In July, a Russian missile entered Polish airspace before landing in a field in eastern Poland. On Wednesday this week, the same day as the fire in Wola Krobowska broke out, a Russian helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace. World.title: Poland and Belarus seek thaw in relations as foreign ministers meet for first time in a decade
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The foreign ministers of Poland and Belarus have met for the first time in a decade, as both sides indicated that they are open to thawing their long-frosty relations. The two countries have regularly clashed in recent years, in particular over Minsk’s alliance with Moscow, the migration crisis Belarus has engineered on the Polish border, and the persecution of Belarus’s ethnic Polish minority. Warsaw, meanwhile, has supported the Belarusian democratic opposition. However, on Tuesday this week, Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski confirmed to reporters that he had met with his Belarusian counterpart, Maxim Ryzhenkov, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Sikorski said that the initiative had come from the Belarusian side. “When a neighbour wants to unfreeze and improve relations, Poland is the first to reach an agreement,” said Sikorski, quoted by broadcaster RMF. “This is a first, introductory meeting, but meetings with other ministries and at other levels are also taking place,” he added, noting that Poland will also “soon be opening a new embassy building in Minsk”. When asked what topics had been discussed, Sikorski said that they had included the border situation and regional security. Asked if he had requested that Belarus not allow Russia to fly drones and missiles through its territory, he said that this was discussed “among other things”. The last known time that the Polish and Belarusian foreign ministers met was in October 2016, when Belarus’s Vladimir Makei visited Witold Waszczykowski in Warsaw. Sikorski said that this week’s meeting with Ryzhenkov had been possible because the situation on their shared border – where Belarus has since 2021 encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants, mainly from Asia and Africa, to cross into Poland – is now “more normalised”. Poland has installed physical and electronic barriers along the border, sent thousands of armed officers to guard it, and has banned asylum claims by migrants who cross irregularly. Following those measures, the number of attempted crossings has fallen dramatically this year. Sikorski also noted that relations have been improved by Belarus’s recent decisions to release political prisoners, including Polish ones. Most prominent among them is Andrzej Poczobut, a leader of the Polish community in Belarus, who had been imprisoned on trumped-up charges for five years. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Minsk’s recent actions have provided “more freedom and greater reasons to try to stabilise relations”, said Sikorski. “A snowdrop can bloom if the weather is favorable.” Belarus’s foreign ministry continued that metaphor in a post on social media on Wednesday, sharing a photo of Sikorski meeting with Ryzhenkov and writing that “snowdrop diplomacy is a nice restart”. “But we’re in it for the harvest,” added the ministry. “Let’s plant an orchard – it needs nurturing every year, not once a decade. Minsk is ready to host.” Last year, Belarus called for “dialogue” with Poland in order to “reduce the risk of armed clashes” amid a military build-up around the border. World.title: Russian military helicopter violates Polish airspace
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Russian military helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace on Wednesday morning, the operational command of Poland’s armed forces has announced. The incident is the latest in a series of airspace violations by Russia, which have also involved drones and, most recently, a missile. It follows recent warnings by the Polish government that Moscow has been planning further “provocations” intended to test NATO’s defences and unity. ❗️ Informujemy, że 23 września br. o godz. 11.08, na północ od miejscowości Braniewo, doszło do krótkotrwałego naruszenia przestrzeni powietrznej Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej przez śmigłowiec Mi-8 Sił Zbrojnych Federacji Rosyjskiej. Śmigłowiec wykonywał lot z Obwodu Królewieckiego.… pic.twitter.com/afULQdSeTc — Dowództwo Operacyjne RSZ (@DowOperSZ) September 23, 2026 On Wednesday afternoon, Polish operational command announced that, shortly after 11:00 a.m. that day, an Mi-8 helicopter belonging to the Russian armed forces had briefly entered Polish airspace near the town of Braniewo, after crossing from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The helicopter did not travel further than 300 metres into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds. In response, the Polish military scrambled fighter jets and placed ground forces on standby. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defences,” wrote operational command. At the time of writing, Russia has not commented on the incident. Today’s violation appears to be the first publicly reported instance of a Russian military helicopter crossing Poland’s land border. Last year, in two separate incidents, a Russian Su-24 bomber and a naval helicopter flew over Poland’s territorial waters in the Baltic Sea. In 2023, two helicopters belonging to the armed forces of Belarus, a close ally of Russia, briefly entered Polish airspace before crossing back over the border. On one night in September last year, around 20 Russian drones entered Poland over its eastern borders amid Russian attacks on Ukraine. Polish and allied forces shot down some of them, while others hit the ground without causing casualties. In July this year, a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile carrying a significant explosive payload entered Polish airspace before landing in a field in eastern Poland. The object that crashed in the Lublin region on Thursday was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile carrying a "significant amount" of explosive material. The missile was "potentially very dangerous,” Poland's defence ministry confirmedhttps://t.co/NoqZwIcaWp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 In recent months, Poland and other NATO countries have been warning of Russian plans to carry out further “provocations” intended to test the alliance’s defences and unity, saying that they could include border and airspace violations. In the last few weeks, Poland has regularly intercepted Russian aircraft that have flown close to Polish territorial waters in the Baltic Sea. This month, Russian drones have repeatedly hit targets in Ukraine near to the Polish border, including a passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw. Just last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that, according to intelligence sources, Russia is planning drone and missile strikes on eastern NATO countries, which it would present as accidental. World.title: Senior Polish presidential official detained amid probe into misspending of funds
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Agents from Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) have detained a senior official from opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki’s chancellery as part of a probe into alleged misspending of funds under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. An employee of a major right-wing broadcaster, Republika, was also taken into custody as part of the same investigation, which relates to the activities of the Polish National Foundation (PFN), a body created under the PiS government to promote Poland abroad but which was also used to further the party’s political interests. Dzisiaj rano w Warszawie na polecenie Prokuratury Regionalnej w Rzeszowie agenci @CBAgovPL zatrzymali Piotra M. i Annę P. ▶️ Zatrzymane osoby przewożone są do @Prok_Regio_RZE, która prowadzi śledztwo dotyczące nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej. ▶️ Na tym etapie… — Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) September 23, 2026 On Tuesday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for the security services, announced that two individuals, named only as Piotr M. and Anna P. under Polish privacy law, had been detained by the CBA at the request of prosecutors investigating irregularities in the PFN. Both suspects previously worked in the chancellery of Prime Minister Beata Szydło, who was head of the PiS government from 2015 to 2017. Piotr M. was head of the Government Information Centre (CIR) and Anna P. led the media services department. Anna P. now works for Nawrocki, who was elected as president last year with the support of PiS. She is director of the Presidential Events Office, which organises the president’s schedule. Piotr M. currently works as a commentator for Republika, a station generally supportive of Nawrocki and PiS. Agenci CBA zatrzymali w Warszawie Piotra M. i Annę P. Sprawa dotyczy nieprawidłowości w Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej! pic.twitter.com/e3jw3ekdOA — Iwona Hartwich (@iwonahartwich) September 23, 2026 In 2017, while still working in Szydło’s chancellery, Piotr M. and Anna P. founded a PR company called Solvere. Later that same year, the company was hired to run a prominent and controversial campaign for the PFN called “Fair Courts”, receiving a reported 1.2 million zloty (€275,000) for the project. The PFN had been set up the previous year under Szydło’s government with funding from 17 state-owned companies. Its publicly declared and statutory mission was to promote Poland abroad. However, the “Fair Courts” campaign, which cost around 8.4 million zloty, was run in Poland itself, with material in Polish, and aimed to show the alleged failings of the justice system in Poland in order to justify why controversial reforms being implemented by PiS were necessary. Echoing PiS rhetoric, the campaign suggested that judges saw themselves as a “special caste” and highlighted cases of alleged wrongdoing by individual judges, including one who had been caught stealing a sausage. (The judge in question had not ruled on a case since that incident in 2006 and had died in 2015.) In 2018, a Warsaw court ruled that the “Fair Courts” campaign was inconsistent with the PFN’s statutory goals, saying that not only did the adverts fail to enhance Poland’s image abroad, “on the contrary, they significantly weakened it, creating a negative image of the judiciary based on individual cases”. In February 2025, just over a year after PiS lost power, a newly appointed PFN board accused its predecessors of criminal negligence that caused damages of over 30 million zloty to the foundation’s finances. They notified prosecutors of potential crimes. In July this year, two men who had served as PFN board members at the time of the campaign were detained as part of an investigation into the misspending of the foundation’s funds. At that time, the CBA also announced that it had searched the homes of Anna P. and Piotr M. A senior official under the former PiS government has been charged over alleged misspending of funds. The case relates to a campaign in 2017 that used money meant for promoting Poland abroad to instead advertise PiS's judicial reforms domestically https://t.co/tH64Bekhec — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 15, 2026 Today’s detentions of Anna P. and Piotr M. were welcomed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. He told Polsat News that the “Fair Courts” campaign was a “double scandal” because it was “not only an abuse of public funds, but also for the very clearly malicious purpose” of “attacking the independent judiciary”. Meanwhile, Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, told the media that the authorities intended to find out “who stood behind” the actions of Anna P. and Piotr M., because “it’s hard to believe this was their initiative”. However, Jarosław Olechowski, a senior executive at Republika, condemned the detentions, calling them an act of “political revenge by the Donald Tusk regime for an information campaign exposing pathologies in Polish courts”. At the time of writing, the presidential chancellery had not commented on the detention of Anna P., the head of its events office. Earlier this year, Nawrocki’s deputy chief of staff was charged with ordering the falsification of documents, an accusation he denies. ❗️❗️❗️❗️❗️ Funkcjonariusze @CBAgovPL zatrzymali @Matczuk_ publicystę @RepublikaTV Przewożą go do prokuratury w Rzeszowie. Powodem zatrzymania jest zemsta polityczna reżimu @donaldtusk za kampanię informacyjną pokazującą patologie w polskich sądach — Jarek Olechowski (@OlechowskiJarek) September 23, 2026 The “Fair Courts” campaign was just one of a number of controversial initiatives launched by the PFN under the PiS government. The foundation was regularly accused of spending money to support PiS’s political goals or on seemingly wasteful projects. One of its most famous initiatives involved the purchase of a yacht for almost €1 million, which was renamed “I Love Poland” and sent on an around-the-world cruise to mark the centenary of Poland’s independence in 2018 (though it suffered damage and spent weeks stuck in a port, accruing further costs). In 2021, the Supreme Audit Office (NIK) accused the PFN of violating the law by refusing to provide documents required for an audit. World.title: New US “Fort Trump” military base in Poland “confirmed”, says President Nawrocki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish President Karol Nawrocki says that a planned new permanent US military base in Poland is “confirmed” because his American counterpart, Donald Trump, is “famous for keeping his word”. He also suggested that the new facility will be called “Fort Trump”. Trump himself declared last week that “major progress” was being made towards establishing the base, saying it was thanks to the “bold leadership of my friend, Karol Nawrocki”, who is a conservative ally of the US president. Meanwhile, earlier this week, a Polish deputy defence minister, Stanisław Wziątek, also expressed confidence that the new base would soon be confirmed and said that it could see the number of US troops stationed in Poland rise to around 15,000. President Karol Nawrocki said he hopes the US will finalize plans to establish a permanent military base in Poland and, if it does, the compound will be christened ‘Fort Trump' https://t.co/SB4DOy5Qp1 pic.twitter.com/aPmvl4JoFO — Bloomberg TV (@BloombergTV) September 22, 2026 The US military presence in Poland has become a big issue this year following Washington’s unexpected last-minute decision in May to cancel the rotational deployment of almost 4,000 troops. Shortly afterwards, Trump declared that he would deploy 5,000 additional troops to Poland. In June, Poland formally submitted a request for the US to establish a new permanent US military base on its territory. In a post on his social media platform, Truth Social, last week, Trump announced “major progress” in those plans and said that “if this happens, the location [of the base] will be announced very soon”. He called it a “historic step for our Great US/Polish Alliance”. On Tuesday this week, speaking to Bloomberg during a visit to the US for the United Nations General Assembly, Nawrocki confirmed that plans for the base were at an advanced stage. “The infrastructure is being chosen right now. Consultants from the US have already visited Poland,” he said. “I think that it’s hard for me to give specific dates, but I think that this matter is for sure confirmed because President Trump is famous for keeping his word.” Nawrocki also expressed confidence that “President Trump will personally be able to participate in the inauguration of Fort Trump”. That name, Fort Trump, was first suggested in 2018 by Nawrocki’s predecessor, Andrzej Duda, when, during Trump’s first term, he sought a permanent US base in Poland. Poland’s government, which regularly clashes with the opposition-aligned Nawrocki and has also at times had tense relations with the Trump administration, has not commented on the idea of naming the new base after the US president. However, the government is keen for the project to move ahead, and has been doing much of the legwork on making it happen. Although Poland’s president is commander-in-chief of the armed forces, his position is largely ceremonial, and it is the government that is responsible for implementing policy. On Monday this week, deputy defence minister Stanisław Wziątek told broadcaster RMF that he was “convinced there is full agreement” on establishing the base, with the remaining question being the precise location. Wziątek said that the announcement could be made before November’s midterm elections in the US, as Trump will be keen to encourage Polish Americans to vote Republican. 💬Kiedy poznamy ostateczną decyzję w sprawie stałej bazy amerykańskiej w Polsce? 💬Jestem przekonany, że pan prezydent @realDonaldTrump będzie chciał zrobić wszystko, aby tak decyzja zachęcająca Polaków do głosowania na Republikanów mogła zapaść przed wyborami – Stanisław… pic.twitter.com/uPWkmdGQod — RozmowaRMF (@Rozmowa_RMF) September 21, 2026 The deputy defence minister said that the base would be likely to host between 3,000 and 5,000 US troops, with 4,500 the “most realistic estimate, because that is the size of a brigade”. In total, said Wziątek, Poland hoped to have “around 15,000” US soldiers in Poland, including the roughly 10,000 that have up until now been present on a rotational basis. The minister admitted that the current rotational presence was lower, around 6,500-7,000, following the cancellation of May’s planned deployment. But he said that the figure should “soon” return to the previous higher level. When asked about the cost to Poland of establishing the new permanent US base, Wziątek said it would “definitely be more than 15 billion zloty (€3.4 billion) but will depend on the level of involvement of the United States”. 💬Ilu w tej chwili w Polsce jest żołnierzy amerykańskich? Ilu będzie docelowo rotacyjnych żołnierzy i w stałej bazie? Odpowiada Stanisław Wziątek @MON_GOV_PL w #RozmowaRMF o 7:00 w @Radio_RMF24@RMF24pl @Radio_RMF24 pic.twitter.com/1Zl66upkp8 — RozmowaRMF (@Rozmowa_RMF) September 21, 2026 The US has long been Poland’s most important security partner. In 2023, under President Joe Biden, it established its first permanent military garrison in Poland at Camp Kościuszko in the city of Poznań. The following year, a US missile defence base opened in Redzikowo on Poland’s northern Baltic coast. This week, the mayor of Poznań, Jacek Jaśkowiak, told newspaper Fakt that his city was one of two locations being considered for the planned new US base. Recent Polish media reports have also identified the provinces of Lower Silesia and West Pomerania as potential locations. While the Trump administration has chastised many NATO member states for failing to meet the alliance’s defence spending targets, it has hailed Poland, whose defence budget is one of NATO’s highest in relation to GDP, as a “model ally”. Between 2021 and 2025, Poland was also the largest importer of arms in NATO. Around 44% of those purchases came from the US, including Abrams tanks, Patriot air defence batteries, and HIMARS rocket artillery. One of them has been charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. On Tuesday, the National Prosecutor’s Office announced that the main suspect, who can be named only as Paweł G. under Polish privacy law, had been detained last week by the Internal Security Agency (ABW) and charged by prosecutors with three alleged crimes. Prokurator ze śląskiego wydziału PZ PK przedstawił 17-letniemu obywatelowi Polski zarzut przygotowania zamachu terrorystycznego, którego celem miało być zabójstwo wielu osób. ⬇️https://t.co/bYi6GY3BaR — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) September 22, 2026 The most serious charge, carrying a potential prison sentence of up to 15 years, relates to undertaking preparations to kill a large number of people through a terrorist attack. Prosecutors say that analysis of data from devices belonging to the suspect revealed correspondence concerning the planning of large-scale attacks, including on a school and a mosque, as well as surveillance of targets, acquisition of weapons, and the use of grenades and Molotov cocktails. Poland has a small Muslim community, but one that has grown rapidly in recent years amid high levels of immigration, and now numbers in the tens of thousands. That has prompted protests from some far-right groups, especially in relation to the growth of Islamic places of worship. Nationalists have protested against an Islamic centre in Kraków, saying they "do not consent to the spread of Islam in Poland". However, the city's equality officer has criticised such groups for "artificially fueling fears and instigating conflicts" https://t.co/qNKJJxMQa5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 6, 2026 Paweł G. is also charged with being part of a criminal group that aimed to “commit a terrorist offence, promote Nazi and fascist content, and incite hatred based on national, ethnic, racial and religious differences”. That crime is punishable by up to ten years in prison. The final alleged offence is public incitement of hatred, promotion of a fascist and Nazi system of state, and possession of Nazi and fascist material with the intention to disseminate it through the internet. That crime carries a jail term of up to three years. The suspect, who prosecutors have confirmed is a Polish citizen, has not pleaded guilty to the alleged offences. A court has accepted a request by prosecutors to keep him in detention for three months while the investigation continues. The National Prosecutor’s Office noted that two additional individuals associated with Paweł G. have been transferred to juvenile courts, without providing further information on what offences they are alleged to have committed. However, in a separate statement, the ABW confirmed that they are two 16-year-olds detained last week as part of an investigation into an online group associated with neo-Nazi propaganda and violence. The ABW named the two suspects as Kacper K. and Wiktor Ś., saying that the pair had been in possession of materials relating to Hitler’s Third Reich, Nazism, racism and antisemitism, as well as terrorist attacks, mass killings and lone-wolf gunmen. Kacper K. has been placed in a juvenile detention centre for three months, while Wiktor Ś. was placed in a police holding centre for children for an unspecified period of time. 🚨Zarzut przygotowywania zamachu terrorystycznego. 3⃣ miesiące aresztu. I jest❗️… https://t.co/gxQmY1VTSQ — ABW (@ABW_GOV_PL) September 22, 2026 In their statement, the ABW said that Paweł G., the suspect now charged by prosecutors, was active in the same neo-Nazi Telegram and Discord online messaging groups as Kacper K. and Wiktor Ś. “Some conversations included elements about planning potential attacks,” wrote the agency. “Participants analysed the modus operandi of the perpetrators of terrorist attacks and viewed them as a source of inspiration.” The ABW also revealed that Paweł G. belonged to an extremist group called Atomwaffen Polska and had co-founded another called Bierut Soldier ZNB. World.title: Czech President Warns NATO Allies May Need to Shoot Down Russian Aircraft
World.content:
Czech President Petr Pavel has warned that NATO may eventually need to shoot down Russian aircraft or drones that deliberately violate the alliance’s airspace.

Speaking to Fox News Digital in New York during the U.N. General Assembly, Pavel said Russia was testing NATO’s readiness and could interpret continued restraint as a sign of weakness.

“There might be the time when we will have to shoot down some of these planes or unmanned vehicles that are testing our readiness,” Pavel said.



Pavel said the alliance needs to distinguish between accidental airspace violations and deliberate incursions in which an aircraft ignores warnings to leave.

“If it is deliberate and the violator doesn’t respond to our measures, then we will have to act, because otherwise Russia simply would push further on,” he said.

His comments came after a series of incidents involving Russian aircraft and drones near NATO territory.

On Wednesday, a Russian Mi-8 military helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace after crossing from the Kaliningrad region. According to Poland’s Armed Forces Operational Command, the helicopter travelled around 300 metres into Polish territory and remained there for 42 seconds.

On Thursday, Romania also scrambled two F-16 fighter jets after an unidentified aerial target entered its airspace from the direction of Ukraine. The object later crashed near the country’s border with Ukraine, with no casualties reported.

Pavel said Russia’s actions reminded him of incidents during his time at NATO, when Russian aircraft repeatedly tested the responses of allied forces.

“They are, on one hand, provoking. On the other, testing what will our reaction be,” he said.

In a speech to the U.N. General Assembly on Wednesday, Pavel said Russia’s “aggressive posture poses a direct threat to European security” and warned that the risks were increasing.

The Czech president also questioned whether Russia was genuinely prepared to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine. He said Moscow would need to agree to a ceasefire before entering meaningful negotiations without conditions.

World.title: New Sports Complex Opens in Prague’s Riegrovy Sady
World.content:
A new sports complex has opened in Riegrovy Sady, giving residents of Prague 2 access to a refurbished court, parkour equipment, a climbing wall and an outdoor fitness area.

The facility, next to the TJ Sokol Královské Vinohrady building, was officially opened Tuesday afternoon. The renovation and installation of new equipment cost CZK 8.7 million, excluding VAT.



The site is intended for people of different ages and can be used for several sports. The refurbished court is suitable for football and basketball, while the new equipment includes a parkour area, climbing wall and a small fitness zone.

The project forms part of the district’s longer-term plans for Riegrovy Sady. Officials said the upper section of the park has lacked sufficient space for outdoor sports and exercise.

The sports area occupies land that until last year was used by two unauthorized structures, the Ice Magic ice sculpture exhibition and the Containall sports and cultural center.

The district is also considering a much larger project for the site. A multifunctional hall for sports and cultural events could eventually replace the current outdoor facility.

Petr Janů, deputy chairman of TJ Sokol Královské Vinohrady, previously said the goal was to create a building designed to remain in place for decades or longer.

The project is still at an early stage. Prague 2 plans to discuss the design with local residents, heritage authorities and Prague’s Institute of Planning and Development. An architectural competition is also expected to be held.

World.title: Prague Taxi Drivers Could Be Tested on Czech and Local Geography
World.content:
Prague taxi drivers could soon be required to demonstrate their knowledge of Czech and the city’s geography.

The Chamber of Deputies approved the change on Wednesday as part of an amendment to the Road Traffic Act. The legislation does not automatically introduce testing in Prague or other Czech cities. Instead, it would give municipalities the authority to impose such requirements.



Under the amendment, municipalities could test taxi drivers on their legal rights and obligations, their Czech language skills to the extent necessary for the job, and their knowledge of locations within the municipality that are relevant to taxi services.

The bill now goes to the Senate.

What the new rules could mean for taxi drivers

The issue has been debated in Prague for some time, particularly as the taxi industry has changed with the rapid growth of app-based services.

Pirate Party leader Zdeněk Hřib introduced a more detailed proposal in May. That version included specific provisions defining what drivers could be required to know and what would fall outside the scope of the tests.

For example, the proposal said drivers should not be expected to demonstrate encyclopedic knowledge of Prague’s landmarks. Transport Minister Ivan Bednárik of the SPD, however, argued that the Pirate Party’s proposal had legal shortcomings.

A shorter amendment submitted by ANO MP Patrik Nacher ultimately became the version approved by the Chamber of Deputies.

Supporters of the change say taxi driving has increasingly become a profession with few formal qualification requirements beyond holding a driving licence.

The explanatory report accompanying the legislation argues that the sector has attracted foreign workers who may have limited knowledge of Czech, local traffic rules and the city in which they operate.

Critics, meanwhile, have raised concerns about the potential impact on fares. They argue that additional requirements could increase the cost of entering the profession and eventually lead to higher prices for passengers.

No English requirement in the legislation

The approved amendment refers specifically to knowledge of the Czech language. It does not introduce an English-language requirement, even though some taxi drivers in Prague also have limited English skills.

The legislation would apply to taxi drivers regardless of whether they operate independently or through digital platforms such as Uber and Bolt.

Foreign nationals make up roughly half of Prague’s registered taxi drivers, reflecting the sector’s long-standing reliance on foreign workers and recently arrived migrants.

World.title: More Than 250 People Fall Ill in Salmonella Outbreak at Prague School
World.content:
More than 240 children and 10 adults have developed gastrointestinal symptoms in connection with a suspected Salmonella outbreak at a school in Prague’s Újezd nad Lesy district.

Masaryk Elementary School, which has around 1,100 pupils, is being temporarily closed while health authorities investigate the source of the infection. The school’s kitchen and cafeteria will also undergo thorough disinfection.



Salmonella has so far been confirmed by laboratory tests in four children, according to Petra Batok, a spokesperson for the Prague Public Health Authority. Officials are continuing to investigate how the infection entered the school.

The first cases were reported earlier this week. The largest number of illnesses has been recorded among upper-level pupils and children attending Montessori classes. Classes for those groups were cancelled on Wednesday, while all pupils have been given Thursday and Friday off.

Food samples taken from the school cafeteria have been sent for laboratory testing, with results expected on Friday.

The final number of people affected is not yet known. Health officials are collecting additional information through questionnaires completed by parents and adults who visited the cafeteria.

The Prague public health authorities have described the incident as an epidemic.

Prague emergency services have received 55 calls from people reporting gastrointestinal symptoms in connection with the outbreak.

Twenty patients were transported to hospitals for treatment, while another 24 were examined and treated without being admitted. The remaining people received medical advice by telephone.

Salmonellosis is usually contracted by consuming contaminated food. Common sources include eggs, insufficiently cooked meat, unpasteurized milk and foods containing raw or unpasteurized eggs. Symptoms generally appear between 13 and 36 hours after infection.

World.title: Prague Metro and Tram Disruptions Planned for September 28 Weekend
World.content:
Prague commuters should expect changes to metro and tram services from Saturday, September 26, through Monday, September 28, as maintenance work affects Metro Line C and tram routes in Libeň.

Metro Line C will be suspended between Pražského povstání and Chodov for the entire long weekend. Trains will continue running between Letňany and Pražského povstání, while the southern section between Chodov and Háje will operate as a shuttle service.



Four stations will be affected by the closure: Pankrác, Budějovická, Kačerov and Roztyly. Passengers can use replacement bus XC, which will run between Pražského povstání and Chodov via all four stations.

Hundreds of railway sleepers to be replaced

The closure will allow Prague Public Transit Company (DPP) workers to replace several hundred wooden sleepers with concrete ones.

Once the work is completed, around 17,000 of the approximately 20,000 original sleepers between Florenc and Kačerov will have been replaced.

DPP said the work is scheduled during long weekends because the materials used to secure the new sleepers need more time to harden than a standard weekend allows.

Tram services suspended in Libeň

Tram services will also be disrupted between Palmovka and Ke Stírce from early Saturday morning until 6 p.m. Monday.

Several lines will operate on modified routes. Tram 3 will run via Těšnov, Vltavská, Strossmayerovo náměstí, Výstaviště, Nádraží Holešovice, Hercovka, Ke Stírce, Kobylisy and Ládví before terminating at Sídliště Ďáblice.

Line 10 will run from Palmovka via Balabenka and Arena Libeň jih to Nádraží Libeň, while lines 24 and 95 will terminate at Palmovka.

Replacement bus X3 will operate during the day between Palmovka, Bulovka, Ke Stírce and Kobylisy. Night service will be provided by bus X95, which will continue to Vozovna Kobylisy.

Passengers using Prague public transport over the long weekend should allow extra travel time and check the latest DPP information before travelling.

World.title: Czech Man Jailed 13 Days After Protest on Moscow’s Red Square
World.content:
A judge at Moscow’s Tverskoy District Court sentenced a Czech man to 13 days in jail on Tuesday for staging a protest on Red Square.

Identified as Michal Plamenek, the man was arrested for holding up a sign in English next to Lenin’s Mausoleum on Sunday afternoon, the court’s press service said in a statement.



No details were provided as to what was written on Plamenek’s sign, but the court press service said a judge ruled that the inscription was “aimed at discrediting the Russian Armed Forces.”

Police officers arrested Plamenek because Red Square directly adjoins the Kremlin, where protests are banned. He allegedly refused to listen to a request by officers to accompany them to a police station and resisted arrest.

A judge found Plamenek guilty on three separate administrative counts of discrediting the Russian military, violating protest rules and disobeying a police officer.

He was also fined a total of 60,000 roubles, around CZK 15,000.

The Czech Foreign Ministry said its embassy in Moscow has been providing the detained man with consular assistance from the outset. It declined to comment further because of the sensitivity of the case.

World.title: Gipsy Kings by André Reyes to Perform in Prague This November
World.content:
The legendary Gipsy Kings by André Reyes will perform in Prague this November, bringing their distinctive mix of flamenco guitar, rumba and Latin rhythms to Lucerna Great Hall on November 29, 2026.

Led by founding member André Reyes, the group will perform some of the songs that made the Gipsy Kings famous around the world, including “Bamboleo,” “Djobi Djoba” and “Volare,” alongside newer material.



The concert is being presented by Gotobeat and will begin at 7 p.m. Tickets are online here.

From southern France to the world

The Gipsy Kings’ story began with the Reyes family and their musical roots in the south of France. André Reyes was one of the founding members of the group, which went on to combine traditional flamenco with rumba, Latin rhythms and pop influences.

Their energetic guitar playing and Spanish-language songs helped turn rumba flamenca into an international sound. Tracks such as “Bamboleo” and “Djobi Djoba” became global hits, while their version of “Volare” introduced the group to an even wider audience.

Music associated with the Gipsy Kings has sold more than 60 million records worldwide, making the group one of the most successful international acts to emerge from the flamenco-rumba tradition.

Their music has also appeared in popular culture, including their version of “Hotel California,” which featured in The Big Lebowski.

A new generation of the Reyes family

André Reyes continues the tradition today with Gipsy Kings by André Reyes, performing alongside younger members of the Reyes family.

The current show combines the group’s best-known classics with newer music, including material connected to Nací Gitano, the band’s latest project. The group is also touring internationally in 2026 as part of its Viva el Arte Tour.

For audiences, the concert offers a mix of familiar songs and new material, with the performance centred on the fast-paced guitar playing, percussion and vocals that have defined the Gipsy Kings sound for decades.

Date: Sunday, November 29, 2026

Time: 7 p.m.

Venue: Lucerna Great Hall, Štěpánská 61, Prague 1

Promoter: Gotobeat

World.title: Heating Season Starts Across Czechia as Temperatures Fall
World.content:
District heating plants across the Czech Republic are beginning to supply heat as temperatures drop, with conditions for the start of the heating season now being met in much of the country.

Some plants have already begun providing additional heat during the colder morning and evening hours. The first systems to respond were mainly in mountainous parts of northern and western Czechia and in the Vysočina region.



Other heating plants are expected to gradually start operating in the coming days, depending on local temperatures and weather forecasts.

Since 2010, district heating systems have generally started supplying heat after September 20, although the exact timing varies considerably from year to year.

If temperatures rise again in late September or early October, heating can be suspended. Under the standard rules, heating is normally interrupted when the average outdoor temperature exceeds 13°C for two consecutive days and the forecast indicates that temperatures will continue to rise.

Last winter was colder than average

The previous heating season placed greater demands on heating systems than the years immediately before it.

According to figures from the Czech District Heating Association, the season was 4.9 percent colder than the previous year. It was also 3.2 percent colder than the average of the preceding 15 years.

The colder conditions translated into higher demand for heat, particularly during periods of sustained low temperatures.

Heating costs could increase next year

Households are not currently expected to face a direct increase resulting from a recent change in the interpretation of a fuel tax exemption, but some other users of district heating could see higher costs.

The issue concerns combined heat and power (CHP) generation. This year, the state changed how an existing fuel tax exemption is interpreted, limiting its application to the amount of heat supplied to households.

Heating companies say the change could increase annual heating bills for institutions such as hospitals and schools by tens or even hundreds of thousands of Czech crowns.

World.title: World Press Photo exhibition opens at Biodome in Budapest
World.content:
The World Press Photo exhibition, which opened at the Biodome in Budapest on Thursday, presents the works of 42 award-winning photographers. The Biodome, the event’s home since the exhibition was forced out of the state-run Hungarian National Museum under the previous Fidesz government, is hosting it for the last time.

World Press Photo exhibition opened

The pictures on display depict the most pressing problems of the present, from devastating conflicts and excesses by law enforcement to the climate crisis and the enforcement of women’s rights.

“The reality this exhibition presents from year to year, the reality it reveals and confronts us with, the reality it thrusts before our eyes, is our own reality. It does not have to please us; it’s enough if it makes us think,” Gergely Karacsony, the mayor of Budapest, said in his speech opening the exhibition.

Alongside the World Press Photo material, visitors can again see accompanying exhibitions this year. One exhibition presents the most memorable pictures of the 2026 election by the photojournalists of 24.hu, while a selection of photographs by Sandor Bojar, a former photojournalist of MTI, commemorates the revolution of 1956.

Democracy exists where people can know the reality

Endre Sós, director general of the Budapest Zoo and Botanical Garden, noted that this is the third and final time the Biodome is hosting the World Press Photo exhibition. Karácsony said: “It would be right for the World Press Photo exhibition to find its home in a state museum once more.”

In 2023 the government barred visitors under 18 from the exhibition at the National Museum, ruling that certain photographs violated a law restricting the display of LGBTQ content to minors. In 2024, with no state institution willing to host the exhibition, the city of Budapest offered it a home at the Biodome, a half-finished botanical garden complex in the Városliget.

“Democracy exists where people can not only speak freely about reality but also freely come to know it, and this exhibition, with its own means, does much for that,” the mayor said. “Year after year we must confront the fact that we will not be in a better mood after viewing the year’s best works,” he said. “This is not the fault of the pictures or the photographers but of the world and of all those who have made the world what it is.”

If you missed: Hungarian photographer shows us abandoned Italy through web camera – PHOTOS

World Press Photo exhibition open until November

“Knowledge of reality can help us act to make the world a better place,” Willem van Ee, the ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Budapest, said in his address, stressing the importance of press freedom.

He noted that journalists and photojournalists are working under ever greater pressure, yet they continue their work. The ambassador described journalism as a tremendous force that shows us, among other things, the conflicts in Ukraine, Sudan and Gaza, and the horrors unfolding elsewhere in the world.

The World Press Photo exhibition at the Biodome is open until 8 November. The winners of the 2026 World Press Photo Contest were chosen by an independent jury of 31 professionals from around the world, who reviewed more than 57,000 photographs by 3,747 photographers from 141 countries.

The CIA took spy photos of almost every part of Hungary in the 1960s – now you can check them out for free!

World.title: India and Hungary strengthen cooperation in Ayurveda through establishment of Academic Chair at Széchenyi István University
World.content:
The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of the Republic of India, and Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary, have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the establishment of an “Academic Chair” in Ayurveda at Széchenyi István University.

The MoU was signed on 23 September 2026 to coincide with Ayurveda Day at Embassy of India by Prof. Dr. Eszter Lukács, Vice-President for International Affairs and Strategic Relation and Dr. Angéla Somogyi, Dean of the Faculty of Health and Sports Sciences on behalf of the Széchenyi István University and the Ambassador of India to Hungary on behalf of the Ministry of Ayush.

Photo: Embassy of India, Budapest

The MoU represents an important step in strengthening and developing cooperation between India and Hungary in the field of traditional systems of medicine, with a particular focus on the academic promotion and dissemination of knowledge relating to Ayurveda.

The Academic Chair will function under the Faculty of Sports and Health Sciences of Széchenyi István University and is envisaged as a platform for fostering academic engagement, knowledge exchange and institutional cooperation in the field of Ayurveda.

Photo: Embassy of India, Budapest

The collaboration between ITRA, Jamnagar, and Széchenyi István University will provide opportunities for enhanced interaction between scholars, academics, researchers and students, and contribute to a greater understanding of India’s rich traditional system of medicine in Hungary.

The establishment of the Academic Chair also reflects the growing interest in India’s traditional knowledge systems and holistic approaches to health and well-being, and provides a new avenue for India–Hungary cooperation in the field of healthcare education and research.

Photo: Embassy of India, Budapest

If you missed: India and Hungary strengthen ties as foreign ministers meet in NY

The MoU builds upon the longstanding and multifaceted relations between India and Hungary, particularly in the areas of education, culture, science and technology, and people-to-people exchanges. It underscores the expanding bilateral cooperation through greater institutional and academic linkages.

The Embassy of India in Budapest remains committed to strengthening and expanding India–Hungary academic and institutional cooperation, particularly in the fields of Ayurveda, traditional systems of medicine, education and research. The establishment of the Academic Chair marks a significant step in this direction and is expected to provide a meaningful platform for sustained academic engagement, knowledge exchange and people-to-people connections between the two countries.

World.title: One of Hungary’s most storied newspapers eliminated during the Orbán era will return
World.content:
Népszabadság, one of Hungary’s most storied newspapers, will return on 8 October — precisely a decade after its abrupt closure — as a digital public-affairs outlet and a weekly printed edition, its leadership announced on Thursday via MTI.

A fraught legacy

The statement recalled that Népszabadság, long regarded as a pillar of Hungarian press history, was shut down on October 8, 2016 by its then-owner in collusion with the Orbán government. After 1990 it had established itself as an independent daily and a dominant force in Hungary’s media landscape; its newsroom served as a training ground for generations of journalists, many of whom now hold senior roles at key independent outlets.

Revival conditions and branding

Although the title ceased publication, its intellectual legacy and trademark endured. Relaunching the paper hinged on securing permission to use the Népszabadság brand — a licence unanimously approved by the Népszabadság Association, which unites prominent figures from the modern era of the newspaper.

Format and editorial mission

The renewed Népszabadság defines itself as an online public-affairs news outlet. At https://nszo.hu/, it will cover Hungarian and international politics, society and the economy with background reports, analysis, features and interviews. In addition, a weekly print edition will survey the week’s most important themes and events.

Media group consolidation with Népszava

The group will also incorporate Népszava: its content will appear in the Népszabadság weekly, uniting the two titles’ intellectual legacies on a shared platform.

If you missed our previous articles concerning the Népszabadság suspension:

Demonstrators show solidarity with daily Népszabadság



Freedom House frowns on Népszabadság sale

Ownership and funding

The publisher of the revived Népszabadság is Liberty Press Kft, which also holds publishing rights to Jelen and Népszava. Ninety per cent of the company will be owned by the newly registering 4Sight Media Group Zrt, with the remaining 10 per cent held by Ákos Tóth, the incoming editor-in-chief. 4Sight Media Group Zrt will provide sufficient funding for two years of operations at launch.

The media group was founded by four Hungarian individuals through their corporate vehicles, citing a long-term opportunity in the transformation of Hungary’s media market. They argue that diminishing state influence — described as having “asphyxiated” the sector — could create a new market environment in which a large, effective public-affairs newsroom can be built.

Editorial team and launch details

Asked by MTI, editor-in-chief Ákos Tóth said the paper’s motto would be: “It changes with the world.” His four deputies will be Zoltán Lakner, Brigitta Szabó, Dóra Varga and Gábor Horváth.

Internal documents show Orbán-linked politician and businessman had unlimited power over Hungary’s public media

Tóth said the newsroom would be built primarily on the existing Népszava staff — which has already absorbed many former Népszabadság journalists — and that the 64-page launch weekly will feature public-affairs coverage alongside content largely drawn from Népszava’s Szép Szó supplement. He added that the printed edition’s size would vary according to how successfully advertising space is sold, noting that there is already advertiser interest.

World.title: Former Piarista pupil PM Péter Magyar meets Pope, bears special gifts
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar described his audience with Pope Leo XIV as open and friendly in remarks to journalists on Thursday in Vatican City, following a private meeting with the head of the Catholic Church. The Prime Minister invited the Pope to visit Hungary and presented the Roman Catholic pontiff with a pair of singular gifts.

A day not to be forgotten

“As a former Piarista pupil, today will remain unforgettable for me,” Mr Magyar wrote on his Facebook page of his one-to-one talks with Pope Leo at the Vatican. Departing the audience with the papal blessing, he added that he had recounted events in Hungary over recent years, “and I told him how a politics founded on honesty, genuine human relationships and hard work can succeed.

”Before the meeting, Mr Magyar paid his respects at the tomb of Pope St John Paul II, from whom he adopted the “Do not be afraid!” slogan used at the outset of his political career and whom he regards as an important role model. The Polish-born pontiff, who endured both Nazi and Soviet communist dictatorships, employed the now-famous phrase in his October 1978 inaugural address.

Pope well informed on Hungary

According to MTI, Mr Magyar said the discussions covered changes in Hungary and the challenges facing Hungarians and Europeans alike, whether war or the energy crisis. They also spoke at length about artificial intelligence and the challenges and dangers it poses, he said. He added that they had discussed the situation of the Catholic Church in Hungary, the social, educational and other services provided by the Church, as well as Hungarian Christian traditions.

The Prime Minister said the Pope was very well informed about the situation in Hungary and Central Europe, and about the circumstances of Hungarian minorities living beyond the country’s borders.

Special gifts

With the 70th anniversary of the 1956 revolution and war of independence approaching, Mr Magyar chose gifts for Pope Leo accordingly. One was a graphically rendered, hand-written Italian version of Pope Pius XII’s address delivered on Vatican Radio on 10 November 1956 in connection with events in Hungary; the other was the first, 1974 New York edition of the memoirs of Cardinal József Mindszenty.Before boarding his Wizz Air flight, Mr Magyar also announced that his two sons had accompanied him on the visit at his own expense.

The first gift:

All parties satisfied

Both sides expressed satisfaction at Thursday’s Hungarian-Vatican meetings over the favourable course of bilateral relations and the role of the Catholic Church in Hungary’s life, the Holy See press office said in a statement after Pope Leo XIV received Prime Minister Péter Magyar in private audience, following which the head of government met Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, the Vatican Secretary of State’s secretary for relations with states, MTI reported.

If you missed: V4 leaders in Gödöllő pledge to strengthen cooperation, build on shared interests

According to the briefing, the talks addressed Hungary’s social and economic situation, as well as several matters of mutual interest, including education and the protection of vulnerable Christian communities in various parts of the world.The discussions also touched on current international issues, with particular reference to the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. The parties expressed hope that the international community would show ever greater commitment to promoting peace, the statement read.

World.title: Breaking – Two Hungarian soldiers die while on duty!
World.content:
Two soldiers have died while on duty in recent days, Hungary’s Defence Minister announced on Thursday.

Writing on his Facebook page, Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said a 20-year-old man had taken his own life during his shift for reasons as yet unknown, while a 41-year-old honvéd fell ill during training and died in hospital the following day. “Neither case involved any known medical or psychological problem,” the minister said, adding that an investigation into the circumstances of both deaths was under way, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

He expressed his condolences to the families and comrades of the deceased. The Hungarian Defence Forces and the Ministry of Defence are examining the precise circumstances surrounding the fatalities.

World.title: Oldest Hungarian brokerage delivers grim euro adoption forecast
World.content:
Hungary’s oldest brokerage firm has poured cold water on hopes of early euro adoption, warning that the earliest realistic date for joining the single currency is much later than the Tisza government promised.

Tisza’s 2030 ambition meets scepticism

Following their landslide election victory, Péter Magyar and the Tisza party spoke of introducing the euro possibly even before 2030 if convergence proceeds smoothly. András Kármán, shortly after the win, suggested Hungary could adopt the euro before 2030 provided the Maastricht criteria were met in good order. Even then, several economists cautioned that euro entry was more likely several years later.

Public backs euro, but with caveats

A June Medián poll found three-quarters of Hungarians support adopting the euro, though most insist on thorough preparation first. Only 23 per cent reject the currency outright, a group disproportionately older, less educated and rural. Support is sharply divided along party lines: 92 per cent of Tisza voters favour the euro, compared with just 32 per cent of Fidesz supporters, according to 24.hu.

PM Magyar promised euro by 2030. Now it seems he may not even be prime minister when the new currency will finally be introduced. That is because a Hungarian premier can only serve two terms following the Tisza government’s new rules, so Magyar may remain in his seat only until 2034. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

Tisza campaigned firmly for euro adoption, in contrast to Fidesz. Viktor Orbán, the former prime minister, never ruled out the euro categorically, but his economic programme rested on keeping the forint as Hungary’s currency, allowing his government decisive influence over its exchange rate and related policy goals.

Equilor: Hungarian euro no sooner than 2033

Hungary can introduce the euro no earlier than 2033, with meeting public finance criteria the chief obstacle to eurozone entry, according to analysts at Equilor Investment Plc. Péter Aradványi, lead analyst, told a Thursday press conference in Budapest that while Hungary failed to meet any Maastricht convergence criterion last year, favourable inflation trends and a falling country-risk premium mean the price-stability condition now appears achievable.

He added that Hungary had also made substantial progress on yield convergence, with prospects for sustaining these gains looking favourable. If rapid budgetary consolidation allows entry to ERM‑2, the European exchange-rate mechanism, in 2030, and the mandatory two-year period there is completed without devaluation, euro adoption could occur in 2033 at the earliest, he summarised.

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar and Hungarian National Bank Governor Mihály Varga. Varga could remain in his seat even after the government change. Photo: Facebook/Varga Mihály

Economic outlook: exchange rate, inflation, debt

But this path demands consistent economic and monetary policy, he stressed. Equilor expects growth of around 2.5 per cent over the next two years, state debt falling to 76.5 per cent of GDP, the base rate easing to 4 per cent and the euro trading between 360 and 370 forints.

Aradványi noted that, because of Hungary’s exceptionally high interest burden on public debt by EU standards, the budget is on a forced trajectory in the short term. Successful fulfilment of the deficit criterion will likely depend heavily on adaptation by domestic and foreign companies, with stronger investment activity and efficient use of incoming EU funds contributing to fiscal consolidation that demands minimal growth sacrifice.

If you missed: Hungarian central bank makes a move towards the euro

He pointed out that, alongside the central bank’s lower 2.5 per cent inflation target from 2028, the current pace of price rises can no longer be considered low, which may justify a more cautious monetary easing. This year’s budget deficit is expected to be extremely high at 7.5 per cent of GDP, pushing public debt to 77.5 per cent, and it could still stand at 76.5 per cent in 2028. Equilor says the credibility of the 2027 budget will be the decisive question in coming months, as all three major rating agencies maintain negative outlooks on Hungary’s sovereign debt.

Hungarian euro coin from 2004, the year Hungary joined the EU. The obverse features King Matthias and his wife, Beatrix of Aragon, while the reverse depicts the Phoenix, a Hungarian cargo vessel built for transport on Lake Balaton.

Source: Vatera Source: vatera

In his view, the announced spending cuts are unlikely to suffice; revenue will also need to rise. On the expenditure side, targeted subsidies may be reviewed, while on the revenue side tax increases could become necessary. Equilor considers a 5–6 per cent budget deficit next year more realistic, since overly restraining investment would improve the numbers in the short term but significantly damage potential growth.Analysts expect the prospect of euro adoption to support the Hungarian equity market, chiefly by reducing currency risk and thereby boosting the international appeal of the domestic capital market.
